Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 1:

(p-3320)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

10 - Surat Yunus

It is named after him, peace be upon him, because it contains His saying: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus?﴾ [Yunus: 98]. In it is the ultimate benefit that faith brings, and the harm of abandoning it and delaying it, and this is the highest purpose of the sending down of the Book (said by al-Mahayimi).

This surah is Meccan, except for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So if you are in doubt﴾ [Yunus: 94], the two verses, and His saying: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it﴾ [Yunus: 40], the verse. It has been said that it was revealed concerning the Jews. It has also been said that from its beginning up to the end of the fortieth verse it is Meccan and the rest is Madinan (related by Ibn al-Furs and al-Sakhawi in Jamal al-Qurra').

Its number of verses is one hundred and nine.

(p-3321)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.﴾

﴿Alif Lam Ra﴾ is recited as a series of letters in the manner of enumeration as a challenge, or it is a name of the surah, in which case its position is nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. this surah is named "Alif Lam Ra". The pointing to it (with "these") before its mention is because, by virtue of it being on the wing of remembrance and about to be recited, it has become in the position of the present, as one says: "This is what so-and-so bought." Or it is accusative, with the implied meaning: recite.

The word "these" (tilka) points to it. As for the case where "Alif Lam Ra" is a series of enumerated letters, the presence of its material, which is the mentioned letters, has been treated as the mention of it, so it is pointed to, as if it were said: "These words composed of the same kind as these spelled-out letters..." etc.

As for the case where it is the name of the surah, the pointing to it has been emphasized after the emphasis on fixing its name, or the command to recite it. The sense of distance in the demonstrative is to alert to the lofty rank of the surah in grandeur. Its position is nominative as a subject whose predicate is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book.﴾ As for the case where "Alif Lam Ra" is the subject, it is a second subject, or an appositive to the first. The meaning: these are particular verses of it, rendered by an independent name, and the intended purpose of stating that they are a part of it is to describe it by the excellent attributes and perfect qualities for which it is famed.

By "the Book" is meant either the entire Great Qur'an, even if the whole was not then sent down, by considering its determination and realization in the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He; or the entire Qur'an sent down at that time, which was understood among people at that time.

"Wise" means possessing wisdom. It is described thus because it includes the wondrous branches of wisdom and speaks them, or it is an attribution of the speech with the quality of its owner, or it is a metaphor (isti'arah makniyyah) based on likening the wise Book to something that speaks with wisdom (related by Abu al-Su'ud).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 2:

His statement, exalted is He:

Discussion on the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who believe that they will have a sure standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord"? The disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is clearly a magician."﴾

﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who believe that they will have a sure standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord"﴾ The hamza here is for denying that they should be amazed, and for expressing their amazement at it. He denied this because God's custom has always been to reveal to men in this manner. Their amazement arose from their distance from his station, the incompatibility of their condition with his condition, and the conflict between what he brought and what they believed. "Qadam" (foot) here means precedence (sabq) metaphorically, because it is its cause and instrument, just as "yad" (hand) is used for blessing, "ʿayn" (eye) for a spy, and "ra's" (head) for a leader. Then, precedence is a metaphor for excellence and moral advancement to lofty stations, so it is a metaphor of two levels. Or "qadam" means station, like ﴿a seat of truthfulness﴾ [al-Qamar: 55], by using the thing that resides for the place where it resides. Its idafa to "sidq" (truthfulness) is the idafa of the qualified to the qualifier. Its origin is "qadam sidq," meaning firmly established and secured. In it there is emphasis, by making it the very essence of truthfulness, and an alert that they attained what they attained only through their truthfulness, outwardly and inwardly.

Al-Infisaf said: "The word 'qadam' is not used for this in the context of evil, either because the metaphor is not consistent, or because it is consistent but custom has prevailed in restricting it, as it prevails in the literal sense."

﴿The disbelievers said﴾, and they are the ones who were amazed, "Indeed, this" i.e. the Wise Book, ﴿is clearly magic﴾ [Yunus: 76], i.e. evident. It was also read "lasahir" (he is a magician), with the reference being to the Messenger, may God's blessings be upon him. This is evidence of their helplessness and their acknowledgment, even if they were lying in calling it magic, because amazement first, followed by speech about what is certainly known to be false, even to the opponent himself, is the habit of the helpless and the silenced.

Then the Exalted explained the falsehood of their astonishment and of what they built upon it, and He affirmed the truth of what they wondered at and the soundness of what they denied, by drawing attention to some of the signs that indicate it from the created order and its measured design, and guiding them to knowledge of it with the slightest reminder. So He, glorified is He, said:

(p-3323) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[3] ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember?﴾

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne﴾. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in refutation of the Jahmiyyah:

Abu al-Aliyah said: "Istawa ila al-sama'" means "irtafa'a" (He rose). Mujahid said: "Istawa 'ala al-'Arsh" means "'ala" (He ascended), without likening (tamthil) and without specifying modality (takyif). The Throne (al-'Arsh) is the body that encompasses all existent things, and it is the greatest of created things. As for "al-Ayyam" (the days), it has been said they are like these days, and it has been said each day is like a thousand years.

﴿Arranging the affair﴾ means He decrees and determines, according to what wisdom requires, the affair of all creation. And ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ is an affirmation of His greatness and the might of His majesty, and a refutation of those who claimed that their gods would intercede for them with Allah. ﴿That﴾ is a pointer to the One known through that greatness, meaning: that Great One described by what has been described is ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the One who nurtured you so that you would worship Him. ﴿So worship Him﴾, that is, make Him one in worship. ﴿Will you not remember?﴾ means: will you not reflect even with the least reflection, which would alert you that He alone deserves lordship and worship, not what you worship.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[4] ﴿To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of Allah is true. Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it, that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice. And those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾: i.e., by death or by resurrection. That is, you will not return in the end except to Him, so prepare yourselves for meeting Him. ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾: i.e., truthful. Then He gave the reason for the necessity of the return to Him by His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿Indeed, He originates creation﴾: i.e., from a drop of semen, ﴿then repeats it﴾: i.e., after death, ﴿that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾: i.e., with His justice, or with their own justice and their upholding of justice in their affairs, or with their faith, since it is the upright justice, just as polytheism is great injustice. This last is the most apt reading, for it corresponds to His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water﴾: i.e., of water whose heat has reached its extreme, ﴿and a painful punishment﴾: i.e., a grievous one whose pain penetrates to their hearts, ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾. This is a causal clause for His saying, for the sake of correspondence with His saying. Its meaning is: that He may reward those who disbelieved with a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because of their disbelief. However, He altered the arrangement for the sake of emphasis on their deserving of punishment, by making it a established right for them, as the lam (اللام) in ﴿لِيَجْزِيَ﴾ indicates; and as an alert that the primary purpose of the originating and the repeating is the granting of reward. Punishment occurs incidentally, through their own acquisition (of disbelief), and that He, Exalted is He, undertakes the rewarding of the believers with what expression cannot encompass, because of its magnificence and greatness. For this reason He did not specify it.

Then, Exalted is He, drew attention, for the purpose of inferring His oneness in His lordship, through the signs of His craftsmanship in the two luminaries, following the inference from what had preceded regarding the originating of the heavens and the earth, by His saying, Glorified is He:

(p-3325) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it phases, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. Allah did not create that except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.﴾

﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance﴾ for the worlds, by day. ﴿And the moon a light﴾, i.e., for them by night. "Ḍiyāʾ" (radiance) is stronger than "nūr" (light). ﴿And determined for it phases﴾: the pronoun refers to both of them, with each one of them being understood; or it refers to the moon alone. He singled out what was mentioned for it, because its phases are known and perceptible, because the rulings of the Sharia are tied to it, and because it is the basis of the Arabs' chronology. ﴿That you might know the number of years and the reckoning﴾, i.e., the reckoning of the months and days, of what the interests in dealings and transactions are attached to. ﴿Allah did not create that except in truth﴾, i.e., with consummate wisdom. ﴿He details the signs for a people who know﴾, i.e., He explains the signs, the cosmic (takwīnīyah) or revealed (tanzīlīyah) ones that draw attention to this, for a people who know the wisdom in the origination of beings, so that they infer from that the oneness of their Originator.

Al-Suyūṭī said: This verse is a foundation of the science of timekeeping (al-mawāqīt), of reckoning (al-ḥisāb), of the phases of the moon (manāzil al-qamar), and of chronology (al-tārīkh). Then he drew attention to the argument for His oneness, glory be to Him, also by His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, there are signs for a people who are mindful of Allah.﴾

﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾: that is, in their succession, and in each of them being a replacement for the other. ﴿and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, from the sun, the moon, the stars, the trees, the animals, the mountains, the seas, and other things. ﴿there are signs for a people who are mindful of Allah﴾: that is, there are great signs indicating the oneness of their Originator, the perfection of His power, and the far-reaching extent of His wisdom. He specified "those who are mindful" because they are the ones who benefit from the outcomes of reflecting upon them, for what calls one to consider and reflect is his taqwa of Allah, exalted is He, and his caution regarding the consequence.

(p-3326) Note:

In these verses there is an indication that the One who brought these wondrous signs into being, deposited in them their manifest benefits, perfected every creature's making, made every thing He created good, distinguished man and taught him eloquent speech, is such that it is part of His mercy and wisdom to choose whomever He wills for His message, so that he may convey from Him general laws which define for people their course in purifying their souls, restraining their desires, and teaching them those deeds which are the measure of their happiness and misery in the Hereafter, as He indicated by His saying:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[7] ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us and are content with the life of this world and feel secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs—﴾ [8] ﴿those—their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾ [Yunus: 8] [9] ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds—their Lord will guide them because of their faith; rivers will flow beneath them in Gardens of Bliss.﴾ [Yunus: 9] [10] ﴿Their call therein will be, "Glory to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace," and the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Yunus: 10]

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ means: they do not anticipate the reward. ﴿And are content with the life of this world and feel secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ means: they do not reflect upon them. ﴿Those—their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾ [Yunus: 8] ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds—their Lord will guide them because of their faith﴾ [Yunus: 9] means: by means of it, to their abode, which is Paradise. It was not mentioned explicitly, relying on its being evident and on the soul being drawn to it, especially in light of what preceded concerning the abode of the disbelievers. ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them in Gardens of Bliss﴾ [Yunus: 9] means: beneath their dwellings, or before them.

﴿Their call therein will be, "Glory to You, O Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 10] means: their supplication is this utterance, because "Allah-humma" is a vocative, and its meaning is: "O Allah, we only glorify You," like the words of the devout one: "O Allah, You alone we worship." It is said: da'a yad'u du'a'an wa da'wa (he called, calls, a calling and a call), just as it is said: shaka yashku shikayatan wa shakwa (he complained, complains, a complaint and a complaint). It is also permissible that by supplication is meant worship, and its parallel is the verse: ﴿And I will withdraw from you and what you call upon besides Allah﴾ [Maryam: 48]. ﴿And their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾ [Yunus: 10] means: what some of them greet one another with, or the greeting of the angels to them, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23] ﴿"Peace be upon you"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 24]; or the greeting of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to them, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58]. And (al-tahiyyah, greeting) is honoring with a manifest state; its origin is: "May Allah grant you a good life." And (al-salam, peace) means safety from every disliked thing. ﴿And the last of their call﴾ [Yunus: 10] means: and the conclusion of their supplication is glorification ﴿is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], meaning: they praise Him, Exalted is He.

The intended meaning of the verse is that the supplication and worship of the people of Paradise is their saying: "Glory to You, O Allah, and praise be to You." The choice of expressing "and praise be to You" by the words "and the last" etc. was in observance of the rhyme (fawasil) and out of concern for praise and what accompanies it of sublime attributes, to remind of their referents. The verse indicates the exalted status of this remembrance, since it is the supplication of the people of Paradise and the remembrance of the angels, as they said: ﴿And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. For this reason, its recitation after the opening takbir is recommended.

Al-Razi said: When the people of Paradise were made joyful by the mention of "Glory to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," and witnessed what it contains of safety from calamities and fears, they knew that all these noble states and holy stations were only made easy by the beneficence, bounty and favor of the Real, Glorified is He. Therefore, they occupied themselves with praise and commendation.

When Exalted is He had explained His severe threat, He followed it with what indicates that it is fitting that it be deferred beyond this worldly life, because its occurrence in this world would be like a barrier to the continuation of obligation. So He, Exalted is He, said:

And (al-salam, peace) means safety from every disliked thing. ﴿And the last of their call﴾ [Yunus: 10] means: and the conclusion of their supplication is glorification ﴿is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10], meaning: they praise Him, Exalted is He.

The intended meaning of the verse is that the supplication and worship of the people of Paradise is their saying: "Glory to You, O Allah, and praise be to You." The choice of expressing "and praise be to You" by the words "and the last" etc. was in observance of the rhyme (fawasil) and out of concern for praise and what accompanies it of sublime attributes, to remind of their referents. The verse indicates the exalted status of this remembrance, since it is the supplication of the people of Paradise and the remembrance of the angels, as they said: ﴿And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. For this reason, its recitation after the opening takbir is recommended.

Al-Razi said: When the people of Paradise were made joyful by the mention of "Glory to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," and witnessed what it contains of safety from calamities and fears, they knew that all these noble states and holy stations were only made easy by the beneficence, bounty and favor of the Real, Glorified is He. Therefore, they occupied themselves with praise and commendation.

When Exalted is He had explained His severe threat, He followed it with what indicates that it is fitting that it be deferred beyond this worldly life, because its occurrence in this world would be like a barrier to the continuation of obligation. So He, Exalted is He, said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 11:

(p-3328) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil [consequence] as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them. But We leave those who do not expect Our meeting in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾

﴿And if Allah were to hasten for the people﴾, and they are those who do not expect the meeting with Him, exalted is He, because of their disbelief, ﴿the evil﴾, meaning that which they used to seek to hasten, for they used to say: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 32], and the like of that. ﴿As they seek to hasten the good﴾, i.e., a hastening like their seeking of the good in prayer. ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾, i.e., they would have been made to die and be destroyed. ﴿But We leave those who do not expect Our meeting in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾, i.e., in their misguidance and their polytheism, going back and forth.

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari claimed that the meaning of "their seeking to hasten with the good" is, i.e., His hastening the good for them, and that he placed the first in the position of the second to indicate the swiftness of His response to them and His granting them their request, so that it is as if their seeking to hasten with the good were a hastening for them. In my view, this is a diversion of the noble wording from its apparent sense without any need for it. Nor is there eloquence in it, even though he was followed in it, and the eagerness to make the verbal noun's governing verb match it so that they are of one pattern is not necessary in Arabic, and the evidence for this is abundant.

Al-Razi allowed that "yu'ajjilu" (He hastens) may originally have been "yasta'jilu" (He seeks to hasten). He turned away from it, out of glorifying the Most Holy Majesty above being described with the seeking of haste, so He is described as bringing it about, while people are described as seeking it, since that is more fitting.

Perhaps the more fitting view is that "isti'jalahum" (their seeking to hasten) is a verbal noun for a verb indicated by what precedes it, and the estimate is: "And if Allah were to hasten for the people the evil which they seek to hasten, [He would do so as] their seeking to hasten." It was omitted for brevity, since it is known, and the saying of His exalted: ﴿And man invokes evil as he invokes good﴾ [al-Isra': 11] agrees with it, for it has the same meaning as what is here.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as though he had never called upon Us to [remove] a harm that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they have been doing.﴾

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us﴾ i.e., to remove it and dispel it. ﴿Lying on his side﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the subject of (called), and the lām is in the sense of (ʿalā), i.e., upon his side, meaning reclining. ﴿Or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on﴾ i.e., he continues on his former way. ﴿As though he had never called upon Us to [remove] a harm that touched him﴾ i.e., to remove it. ﴿Thus is made attractive to the transgressors what they have been doing﴾ i.e., of turning away from the remembrance (dhikr) and following desires. This verse is brought as an argument against the polytheists, based on what they were created with, like others, of resorting to Him, Exalted is He, in times of hardship, knowing that none removes them except Him, so that they might cast aside the worship of what neither harms nor benefits, and become certain that He is the One God, besides whom none is to be worshipped. In it is also a rebuke against them for the evil of their turning, after the removal of their distresses, and a warning against the likes of their conduct.

Then, Exalted is He reminded them of the greatness of His power through what has reached them of the news of the former peoples, so that they might fear Him, with His words, glorified is He:

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[13] ﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they committed wrongdoing, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.﴾

﴿And We destroyed the generations before you when they committed wrongdoing﴾ i.e., by denying and disbelieving. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe﴾ i.e., He established the proof against them by many aspects. They were not going to believe in those clear proofs or in anything else, so He recompensed them with the well-known destruction among them. ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people.﴾

(p-3330) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿Then We made you successors in the land after them, that We might observe how you would act.﴾

﴿Then We made you successors in the land after them, that We might observe how you would act.﴾ The address is to those to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, meaning: We appointed you as successors (istikhlaf) in the land after the generations which We destroyed, so that We might observe how you would act, whether in good or in evil, and thereby deal with you according to your deeds.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾

﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾

He, exalted is He, informs of the obstinacy of the disbelievers among the polytheists of Quraysh: when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited to them the Book of God and its clear proofs, they said to him, "Bring a Qur'an other than this," meaning, bring us something of a different form, "or change it" into another arrangement. God, exalted is He, said to His Prophet, ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord,"﴾ meaning, that is not up to me; I am only a conveyer of the message from God, exalted is He.

It has been said: He only answered the matter of changing it, rather than the first demand, to indicate that the impossibility of what they proposed first is so evident that there is no need to explain it. Also, engaging with that, although it is futile, might be considered a form of humoring fools, since such a proposal does not come from people of sound intellect. Furthermore, what indicates the impossibility of the second also indicates the impossibility of the first, by a stronger argument, so the answer covers both matters in terms of outcome and reality. His saying, ﴿if I disobey my Lord﴾ means, by changing it and abrogating it (naskh, abrogation) of my own accord.

al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): "It was used as evidence by those who prohibited the abrogation of the Qur'an by the Sunnah." End of quote.

al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: what was their aim, though they were the most cunning and deceitful of people in this proposal? I say: it was plotting and deceit. As for the proposal to replace one Qur'an with another, it implies that it is from you, and that you are able to produce its like, so he would replace it with another. As for the proposal of change and alteration, it was out of greed and to test the situation, and that if any alteration came from him, either God would destroy him and they would be rid of him, or He would not destroy him and they would mock him and make the alteration a proof against him and a confirmation of his fabrication against God." End of quote.

When He had clarified the falsehood of what they proposed to bring and its impossibility, He pointed to establishing the truth of the Qur'an and that it is from Him, exalted is He, in His saying:

**The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:**

[16] ﴿Say: "If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you through me. I had already lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?"﴾

﴿Say: "If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you"﴾

Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that its recitation is only by the will of God and His bringing into being a wondrous matter that goes beyond customary practice. This is that a man who is unlettered, who has not learned and has not listened, who has not seen the scholars for a single hour of his life, and who did not grow up in a land where there are scholars, should come forth and recite to you a book of eloquence that overwhelms every eloquent speech and rises above every prose and poetry, filled with knowledge of the fundamentals (*usul*) and the derived rulings (*furu'*), and reports of what has been and what will be, speaking of the unseen matters that none knows but God. He has lived among you for forty years, and you have observed his circumstances, and nothing of his secrets has been hidden from you. You have not heard from him a single letter of this, and no one among the people closest to him and most attached to him has known it from him.

(p. 3332) ﴿Nor would He have made it known to you through me﴾, that is, nor would He have informed you of it through my tongue. ﴿I had already lived among you a lifetime before it﴾, that is, before its descent. I did not engage in anything related to its like, nor was I known for knowledge and eloquence, so that you could accuse me of inventing it. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾, that is, so that you would know that it is none other than from God, and not from one like me.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a reply to what they inserted beneath their saying, "Bring a Qur'an other than this," by way of attributing fabrication to him.

**Note:**

Abu al-Su'ud held that the more fitting basis for the reply in what preceded is the mere impossibility of his issuing any alteration or substitution, since that would be a disobedience entailing a great punishment, and the restriction of his state, peace be upon him, to following revelation and refraining from arbitrary opinion. Without addressing it there or here, because the Qur'an in itself is a matter beyond human capacity, and not because he, peace be upon him, was unable to produce its like, he cites here, in support of the claim, what befits this from his continuous circumstances during that long period: his complete purity from anything that suggests the slightest lie or fabrication against anyone whosoever. This is as indicated by its being followed by the description of the one who fabricates against God as a wrongdoer.

The meaning is: I have lived among you before the revelation, never confronting anyone with arbitrary domination or disputation, and never hovering around a statement containing any trace of doubt, let alone one containing a lie or fabrication. Will you not reason that one whose condition has been consistently so in this long period is impossible to fabricate against God and to impose domination over all creation with commands and prohibitions that necessitate the shedding of blood, the seizing of wealth, and the like? And that what he brought is a clear revelation, a descent from the Lord of the worlds. (End.)

What he (may God have mercy on him) found fitting, Ibn Kathir also limited himself to, and then cited the words of Heraclius, king of the Romans, to Abu Sufyan, in what he asked him about the description of the Prophet ﷺ. Heraclius said to him: "Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" Abu Sufyan said: "I said, no!" Abu Sufyan at that time was the head of the disbelievers and the leader of the polytheists, and despite this he acknowledged the truth.

(p. 3333) *Excellence is what the enemies bear witness to.*

Heraclius then said to him: "I know that he would not have left lying to people only to lie against God."

Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said to al-Najashi, king of Abyssinia: "God sent among us a Messenger whose truthfulness, lineage and trustworthiness we know. The length of his stay among us before prophethood was forty years."

It is related from Ibn al-Musayyib: "Forty-three years." The sound and well-known report is the first.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 17:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[17] ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ [17].

﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial (istifham inkari), whose meaning is negation. That is: there is no one more wrong than one who fabricates speech against Allah, the Exalted, and claims that He sent him and revealed to him, or who disbelieves in His signs, as the polytheists did by denying the Qur'an and claiming that it came from him (ﷺ) of his own accord.

﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ That is, they will not be saved from what they fear, nor will they attain what they seek. A parallel to this verse is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah, or says, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing has been revealed to him, or who says, "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down"?﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. The ordering of the non-success of one who fabricates revelation is a true promise without doubt, for its fabricator will bear disgrace and punishment, and his matter will not be unclear to anyone in any state.

It is mentioned that 'Amr ibn al-'As visited Musaylimah the liar, and he had been a friend of his in the pre-Islamic period, and 'Amr had not yet embraced Islam. Musaylimah said to him: "Woe to you, 'Amr! What has been revealed to your companion (meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) during this period?" He said: "I heard his companions reciting a great, short surah." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "﴿By time﴾ [al-'Asr: 1] ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr: 2], etc." So Musaylimah thought for a while, then said: "And there has been revealed to me something like it!" He said: "And what is it?" He said: "O Wabr, O Wabr! You are only two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is a scrambling burrow. How do you see it, O 'Amr?" 'Amr said to him: "By Allah! You know that I know that you are indeed a liar."

'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, the people rushed toward him, and I was among those who rushed toward him. When I saw him, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him say was: 'O people! Spread the greeting of peace, feed the food, maintain the ties of kinship, and pray at night while people are asleep; you will enter Paradise in peace.'" Hassan said:

Had there been no clear signs in him, his readiness would have brought you news.

The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[18] ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them﴾ That is, the idols, which are inanimate objects (jamad) that cannot bring benefit or harm; i.e., it is part of the nature of a deity to have the power to do so. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ That is, do you inform Him that they are His intercessors? This is an informing about something that is not known to Allah, and if it is not known to Him—He being the All-Knowing who encompasses all that is known—then it does not exist. Thus it is a report that has no one to report it.

If you ask: how did they inform Allah of this? I say: it is a mockery of them and of what they claimed, namely the impossibility of the intercession of idols, and an indication that what they informed Him of is false. It is as though they were informing Him of something whose knowledge is not connected to Him, just as a man is informed of something he does not know.

His words ﴿in the heavens or on the earth﴾ are an emphasis on its negation, because whatever is not found in them is negated and nonexistent—so said al-Kashshaf. ﴿Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾ That is, exalted above the partners they ascribe to Him, or above their associating [others with Him].

Then He, exalted is He, pointed out that monotheism and submission (Islam) are an ancient creed upon which all people were, both by innate nature (fitrah) and by legislation (tashri'), with His words:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[19] ﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed. And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord, the matter would have been decided between them concerning that wherein they differ.﴾

﴿Mankind was but one community﴾: that is, upright (ḥunafāʾ), agreeing upon one religion, which is the natural disposition of Islam and monotheism (tawḥīd), the disposition upon which every person is created. ﴿Then they differed﴾ by following desires and worshipping idols. Polytheism (shirk) and its branches are ignorances invented by the misguided, diverting people from the direction of monotheism. For this reason God sent the Messengers with His signs and His conclusive proofs, so that whoever perished would perish after a clear proof, and whoever lived would live after a clear proof. ﴿And were it not for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾: that is, by deferring the judgment between them until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾: that is, immediately, ﴿concerning that wherein they differ﴾, by distinguishing truth from falsehood, preserving the one who is right and destroying the one who is wrong.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿They say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The unseen belongs only to God, so wait; I am waiting with you."﴾

﴿They say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ That is, one of the signs they proposed out of obstinacy and stubbornness. They did not value the great and abundant signs that had been sent down to him, the like of which had not been sent down to any of the prophets. The Qur'an alone suffices as a sign that remains throughout time, unique and wondrous among signs. ﴿Say, "The unseen belongs only to God"﴾ That is, He alone has exclusive knowledge of the unseen, and He alone holds it. Neither I nor anyone else has knowledge of it. The meaning is that what prevents the sending down of the signs they have proposed is a hidden matter, which none knows but Him.

﴿So wait; I am waiting with you.﴾ That is, wait for what God will decree concerning the outcome of your obstinacy, for the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing. God, exalted is He, has said in another verse: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ [al-Isra: 59]. And He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe﴾ [Yunus: 96], ﴿even if every sign should come to them﴾ [Yunus: 97]. And He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a written scripture on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is not but obvious magic"﴾ [al-An'am: 7]. That is, such people are less deserving than to be granted their proposal, because of the extreme intensity of their obstinacy.

It is not hidden that the noble Qur'an, since the compelling proof of the truthfulness of his prophethood, peace be upon him, has been established by its inimitability, the demand for another sign besides it, of the kind they propose, is unnecessary for the soundness of his prophethood and the confirmation of his mission. Such signs are left to His will, exalted is He, and are referred to His unseen knowledge. Whether they are sent down or not, his prophethood has already been established and his mission has been made clear, may the blessings of God be upon him.

(p-3337) Then God, exalted is He, emphasized their stubbornness and obstinacy, indicating that they would not submit even if their proposal were granted, by what is known of them of turning away from Him after He removes their harm, to associating partners with Him, in His saying:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[21] ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they have a scheme against Our verses. Say: "Allah is swifter in planning." Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot.﴾

﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them﴾ meaning: it mingled with them until they felt the evil of its effect upon them. ﴿Behold, they have a scheme against Our verses﴾ meaning: their scheming becomes manifest and the hidden part of their polytheism appears. So at the time of adversity they turn sincerely toward Him, seeking its removal, like the deceiver who displays the opposite of what he conceals, and then his matter becomes clear afterward. ﴿Say: "Allah is swifter in planning"﴾ meaning: swifter in punishment. That is, His punishment arrives to you more quickly than what you contrive in repelling the truth. The naming of punishment as "planning" is because it comes in correspondence to their planning, whether in actuality or in mention. ﴿Indeed, Our messengers﴾ meaning: those who guard your deeds ﴿record what you plot﴾ meaning: your scheming, or what you scheme, and this is a confirmation of the retribution and a warning that what they devised to conceal is not hidden from the guardian angels, let alone from the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

Then the Exalted explained a kind of their scheming in the verse of their deliverance from the深 depths of the sea, with His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea, until when you are in the ships and they sail with them on a pleasant wind and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion: "If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

﴿It is He who enables you to travel﴾ i.e., the ships (p-3338) ﴿and they sail﴾ i.e., the ships ﴿with them﴾ i.e., with those who are in them ﴿on a pleasant wind﴾ i.e., one gentle in its blowing, agreeable to what is desired ﴿and they rejoice in it﴾ because of the safety from the dangers ﴿a violent wind comes upon them﴾ i.e., one of great force ﴿and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed﴾ i.e., the causes of destruction surround them, which are the severity of the waves and the wind ﴿they call upon God﴾ i.e., to be delivered from them ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾ and this is the supplication, because at that time they do not call upon anyone besides Him with Him ﴿"If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful"﴾ i.e., among those who worship You with gratitude.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[23] ﴿So when He had delivered them, behold, they were committing outrage in the earth without right. O mankind, your outrage is only against yourselves—the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

﴿So when He had delivered them, behold, they were committing outrage in the earth without right﴾ means: they were corrupting therein, and hastening toward what they had been upon of shirk and the like. ﴿O mankind﴾ means: O you who forget the blessing of deliverance through sincere devotion and the answering of supplication. ﴿Your outrage is only against yourselves﴾ means: its harm falls upon you. ﴿The enjoyment of worldly life﴾ is a omitted predicate, or it is "enjoyment" itself; or it is a second predicate; or it is the predicate of "your outrage," with ﴿against﴾ ('ala) being related to it. It has also been read in the accusative (naṣb) as a verbal noun (maṣdar) of an omitted verb, meaning: "We grant you enjoyment"; or as a direct object (maf'ul bihi) of it, meaning: "you seek." ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ means: in the worldly life; and this is a threat of their recompense for outrage.

(p-٣٣٣٩)The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[24] ﴿The likeness of the life of this world is only like water which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it, from which men and livestock eat, until when the earth has taken on its adornment and become beautified, and its people think that they have power over it, Our command comes to it by night or by day, and We make it into stubble as though it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who give thought.﴾

﴿The likeness of the life of this world is only like water which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it﴾: that is, it was mixed with it because of its penetration into it. The *ba'* (بِ) here indicates accompaniment (lil-musahabah), or it indicates causation (lil-sababiyyah), meaning that it mixed through its means, until some of it mixed with other parts, that is, some of it intertwined with other parts. The first is more apparent. ﴿from which men and livestock eat﴾: of crops, fruits, herbage and grass. ﴿until when the earth has taken on its adornment﴾: that is, its beauty and splendour. ﴿and become beautified﴾: that is, with the various kinds of vegetation. ﴿and its people think that they have power over it﴾: that is, they are able to gather its grains and fruits and harvest it. ﴿Our command comes to it﴾: that is, Our punishment. ﴿by night or by day﴾. ﴿so We make it into stubble﴾: that is, like something reaped from its root. ﴿as though it had not flourished﴾: that is, as though it had not grown. ﴿yesterday﴾: that is, shortly before that time. "Yesterday" (al-ams) is an example of a near time. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾: that is, through examples, bringing them close. ﴿for a people who give thought﴾: that is, upon their meanings.

Note:

Al-Qashani said: *al-baghy* (البَغْيُ, oppression, transgression) is the opposite of *al-'adl* (justice). Just as justice is a comprehensive virtue encompassing all virtues, and a unified disposition belonging to it, emanating upon the soul from the light of unity, oppression does not occur except from the utmost immersion in vices, such that it necessitates all of them together. It thus accompanies them at the furthest distance from the truth and the ultimate darkness, as He said: "Darkness upon darkness on the Day of Resurrection." Therefore He said: "against yourselves" and not "against the one oppressed," because the one oppressed is made happy through it, while the oppressor is made utterly wretched. And this is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world, since all the excesses and deficiencies opposed to justice are natural pleasures and animal delights, which end with the ending of sensory life. He illustrated this with the swiftness of its passing and the brevity of its duration, through this example He gave of the earth's adornment with its splendour from the rainwater, then its ruin by some calamities swiftly before benefiting from its vegetation, followed by everlasting wretchedness and painful, perpetual punishment.

In a hadith: "The swiftest of good deeds in reward is the maintenance of kinship ties, and the swiftest of evils in punishment is oppression and a false oath," because its perpetrator accumulates the rights of people upon him, so his punishment cannot bear the long delay that the right of God Exalted can bear. End of quotation.

I heard some of the shaykhs say: The oppressor and the sinner rarely reach the age of old age, because they wage war against God Exalted by demolishing the order whose care God Exalted has directed toward its preservation, and by opposing Him in His wisdom and justice. End of quotation.

When God Exalted mentioned the world and the swiftness of its passing, He encouraged toward Paradise and called to it, and named it the Abode of Peace (Dar al-Salam), that is, free from calamities and deficiencies, contrasting the world, which is exposed to calamities as already explained. So He, glorified is He, said:

(p-٣٣٤١) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ [26] ﴿For those who have done good is the best (reward) and more. Neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ [Yunus: 26]

﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace﴾ means He calls creation, through His Oneness (tawhid), to His Paradise. ﴿And guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ means to a upright religion (din qayyim) that He is pleased with, which is Islam.

﴿For those who have done good is the best (reward) and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. That is, for those who have done good in their consideration (husn al-nazar), so they recognized the deception of this world and its desires, turned away from them, and directed themselves to God Exalted, worshipping Him as though they see Him. The best reward is Paradise, and "more" beyond the reward is bounty (tafaddul), as He Exalted said: ﴿and He will increase them from His bounty﴾. The greatest form of this is looking upon the Noble Face of God Exalted. Therefore, its interpretation as the vision (of God) has been widely transmitted from more than one of the Companions (sahaba) and the Successors (tabi'un). Ibn Jarir traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ), through Abu Musa, Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, and Ubayy. Ibn Abi Hatim did likewise.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿For those who have done good﴾ [Yunus: 26], etc., and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise! Indeed, you have a promise with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you.' They will say: 'What is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us into Paradise, and removed us from the Fire?' He said: Then the veil will be lifted for them, and they will look at Him. By Allah! Allah has given them nothing more beloved to them than looking at Him, and nothing more soothing to their eyes." Muslim also narrated it in this form.

(p-٣٣٤٢) ﴿Neither darkness will cover their faces﴾ [Yunus: 26], that is, no black dust from the love of this world and its desires will cover them. ﴿Nor humiliation﴾ [Yunus: 26], that is, a trace of disgrace and the dimming of gloom, resulting from turning toward what is other than God Exalted.

Al-Nasir said: In the juxtaposition of "more" (ziyada) with this clause there is confirmation of the correctness of interpreting "more" as the noble vision, for it contains an indication of the honouring of their faces by looking at the Face of God Exalted. It is therefore fitting that the darkness of distance and the humiliation of the veil should not cover their faces, unlike the deprived and veiled, whose faces are covered with the darkness of rejection and the humiliation of distance.

His saying Exalted: ﴿Those﴾ [Yunus: 26], that is, those who have done good, ﴿are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally﴾ [Yunus: 26].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 27:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Those who have earned evil deeds—the recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿Those who have earned evil deeds﴾, i.e., polytheism (shirk) and sins (ma'asi). ﴿The recompense of an evil deed is its equivalent﴾ ﴿and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah﴾, i.e., no shield that would protect them from the punishment. ﴿It is as if their faces were covered﴾, i.e., clothed, ﴿with pieces﴾, i.e., portions, ﴿of the dark night﴾, owing to the intensity of their blackness and darkness. This is because of their committing the dark condition of the natural excretions (al-muyul al-tabi'iyyah) and the vile deeds, and the purpose is to inform, by the most striking of comparisons, about the blackness of their faces. This meaning has been mentioned in more than one verse. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Then He, exalted is He, explained what the polytheists would suffer on the Day of Gathering of reproach and disgrace, by His saying:

The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿And the Day We gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them, and their partners will say: "You did not used to worship us."﴾

﴿And the Day We gather them all together﴾ meaning the polytheists and what they worshipped, for the exchange of words between them. ﴿Then We will say to those who associated others with Allah﴾ i.e., to their deities besides Allah, while they still expected intercession from them. ﴿Stay in your place, you and your partners﴾ i.e., remain in your places, do not depart until you see what will be done to you. Al-Qashani said: its meaning is: "Stand where you stood in the station, in severing the bonds and the causes that were the reason for your love and worship, and the disavowal of the worshipped from the worshipper due to the cessation of the natural motives that necessitated those bonds."

As for His saying ﴿and We separated them﴾, its meaning is: although they are together in the station, We separate them and sever the bonds that were between them, so no worshipper retains any expectation of intercession, nor do the worshipped retain the ability to grant it, even if they were able to. ﴿And their partners will say: "You did not used to worship us"﴾, since your worship was not by our command, but by the command of Satan. Thus you were in truth worshippers of him, by your obedience to him, and worshippers of what you invented in your imaginations of false falsehoods and lying wishes.

It has been said: the saying is a figure of speech for their disavowal of their worship, and that they worshipped their desires and their devils, because these are the ones who commanded them rather than them (the idols), since idols are inanimate and do not speak. And it has been said: Allah, who makes everything speak, will make them speak, so they will address them with that, in place of the intercession they used to expect.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you. Indeed, we were unaware of your worship of us.﴾

﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you. Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾ — that is, of us (lana). ﴿Unaware﴾ — that is, Allah knows that we did not command you to that, nor did we intend your worship of us.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿There, every soul will experience what it has sent before, and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will be lost to them.﴾

﴿There﴾ means in that astonishing station, at the time of the severing of ties and the denial by the partners of worship, ﴿every soul will experience what it has sent before﴾, meaning every soul will test and taste the deeds it sent ahead, and will witness their effects, whether ugly or beautiful, rejected or accepted, just as a man tests a thing and comes to know it in order to learn its true state. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and what he left behind﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13], and His saying: ﴿On the Day when hidden things are examined﴾ [al-Tariq: 9].

﴿And they will be returned to God, their true Master﴾: the pronoun refers to those who associated partners with God, meaning they will be returned to God, who dispenses their recompense with justice and equity. ﴿And what they used to fabricate will be lost to them﴾, meaning what they had invented, the foundations of their religion and their creed, their false imaginings, and their vain wishes will be lost to them and perish. That is, their loss and misguidance will become manifest, and no trace of them will remain among them.

In this verse there is severe rebuke of the polytheists who worshipped what neither hears, nor sees, nor avails them anything. God did not command them to do so, nor was He pleased with it, nor did He will it; rather, He disowned them at a time when they most needed help. The polytheists are of various kinds and categories, and God has mentioned them in His Book, explained their conditions, and refuted them with the most complete refutation.

Then He argued against the polytheists for His oneness, by their acknowledgment of His lordship alone, in His words, glorified and exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 31:

(p-3345) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who arranges the affair?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾

﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"﴾ By sending down rain and causing growth. And can this be done except by One who has general control over them?

﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ That is, who is able to create them both and to shape them according to the wondrous natural form upon which they have been fashioned? Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "He is the One who brought you into being and made for you hearing and sight."﴾ [al-Mulk: 23]

﴿And who brings the living out of the dead?﴾ meaning the living soul out of the sperm-drop, or the bird out of the egg, or the ear of grain out of the seed. ﴿And brings the dead out of the living?﴾ such as bringing the sperm-drop out of the human being, and the egg out of the bird. It was also said: the intended meaning is bringing the believer out of the disbeliever, or the disbeliever out of the believer.

﴿And who arranges the affair?﴾ That is, who takes charge of arranging the affair of the entire world, in whose hand is the dominion of everything? This is a generalization after a particularization.

﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾ since there is no room for obstinacy given how clear this is.

﴿So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ That is, will you not fear, after your acknowledgment, His wrath for worshipping other than Him, following your desires?

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[32] ﴿So that is Allah, your Lord, the Truth. And what is there after the truth except error? So how are you turned away?﴾

﴿So that is﴾ is a reference to the One whose power and actions are such. ﴿Allah, your Lord, the Truth﴾ — the One whose oneness is established with a firmness beyond any doubt, for whoever examines carefully. ﴿And what is there after the truth except error?﴾ meaning: truth and error have no intermediate state between them. Whoever goes beyond the truth falls into error. That is, after the truthfulness of His lordship there is nothing but the invalidity of the lordship of anything other than Him, and the worship of other than Him, whether alone or in association. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾ That is, away from the truth, which is tawhid (divine oneness), toward error, which is shirk (association of partners with Allah), while you yourselves acknowledge that He is the Creator of everything.

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

﴿Thus has the word of your Lord come true against those who defied, that they will not believe.﴾

That is, His judgment and decree were confirmed against those who persisted in their disbelief and went to the utmost extreme in it. His saying ﴿that they will not believe﴾ is an apposition (*badal*) to "the word": that is, it was decreed against them that faith would not be attained, and God knew this about them. Or He meant by "the word" the promise of punishment, and ﴿that they will not believe﴾ is a causal clause, in the sense of "because they will not believe," as al-Zamakhshari stated. This is like His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers."﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], and His saying: ﴿Is it then the one against whom the word of punishment has come true [that] you can save who is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19].

It has been said: ﴿those who defied﴾ is an explicit noun placed in the position of the pronoun of the addressees, to indicate causation. Here "*al-fisq*" (defiance) means persistence in disbelief. The sense thus comes to this: the word of punishment came true against them because of their persistence in disbelief and because they will not believe. This is a repetition. It has been answered that it is an explicit statement of what was understood implicitly from ﴿those who defied﴾, or a indication of the nobility of faith, namely that the punishment of those who persist in disbelief is due to the absence of faith.

Then He also argued, for the truth of monotheism and the falsehood of association (*shirk*), by means of what is among His exclusive attributes, from the beginning of creation and its return, so He said, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?" Say: "It is Allah who originates creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded away?"﴾

﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?"﴾ That is: who begins it from a drop of semen, places in it the soul so that it may know Him, employs it in deeds, and then revives it on the Day of Resurrection, so that He may recompense it for what it sent forward (p-3347) in its past days. The resurrection has been placed within the frame of argument although they do not acknowledge it, as a notification of the manifestness of its proof through the evidences that establish it, by transmitted text and by reason, and that denying it out of obstinacy and stubbornness is not to be heeded; and as an indication that the origination and the resurrection are mutually entailed in existence and non-existence, so that acknowledging the one necessitates acknowledging the other. Then he, upon him be prayer and peace, was commanded to make clear to them who does that, and it was said to him: ﴿Say: "It is Allah who originates creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded away?"﴾ That is: how are you turned away toward worshipping another, when he is incapable of what has been mentioned? Then He argued against them again, silencing them one refutation after another, with His words, exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[35] ﴿Say, "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?" Say, "Allah guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who does not find guidance unless he is guided? So what is wrong with you? How do you judge?"﴾

﴿Say, "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?"﴾ That is, in any way whatsoever, such as sending the messengers, granting intellect, enabling contemplation of the signs of the cosmos, and granting success in reflection. ﴿Say, "Allah guides to the truth. Is He who guides to the truth﴾ — and He, blessed and exalted, is the one who guides — ﴿more worthy to be followed﴾ — that is, worshipped and obeyed — ﴿or one who does not find guidance﴾ — that is, unless Allah guides him. Here the idols are treated as if they were rational beings, in order to confound them. It was also said that its meaning is: or one of the idols who cannot find its way to a place so as to move to it, unless it is moved; or one who does not find guidance and for whom guidance is not possible, unless Allah transforms its state by making it a living, responsible creature, and then guides it. It has been read ﴿أمَّنْ لا يَهَدِّي﴾ with a fatḥah on the yāʾ and the hāʾ and a shaddah on the dāl; its original form is يَهْتَدِي (yahtadī), the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl (idghām), and the fatḥah of the assimilated tāʾ was transferred to the hāʾ. It has also been read with a fatḥah on the yāʾ, a kasrah on the hāʾ, and a shaddah on the dāl, because when the vowel was transferred, two consonants with sukūn came together, so the first of them was given a kasrah to avoid their meeting. It has further been read with a sukūn on the hāʾ and a lightened dāl, in the sense of (يَهْتَدِي). The Arabs say يَهْدِي meaning يَهْتَدِي; it is said: هَدَيْتُهُ فَهُدِيَ, i.e., اهْتَدَى.

And His saying, ﴿So what is wrong with you﴾, is a subject (mubtada′) and predicate (khabar), and the interrogative is for denial and wonder. That is: what is it with you in taking as partners these ones who are incapable of guiding themselves, let alone guiding others? And His saying, ﴿How do you judge?﴾ is a resumptive new sentence (istiʾnāf), meaning: how do you judge falsely, in that you claim they are equals of Allah?!

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[36] ﴿And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

﴿And most of them follow﴾ — that is, in their belief in the divinity of the idols. ﴿nothing but conjecture﴾ — a belief not supported by any proof, but rather by empty fancies and corrupt analogies. What is meant by "most" (al-akthar) is all of them. ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ — that is, against knowledge and true belief. ﴿nothing﴾ — that is, of granting sufficiency. So "shay'an" (nothing) is in the place of a verbal noun (masdar), meaning "any sufficiency at all." Or it is an object of "yughni" (avails), and "min al-haqq" (against the truth) is a circumstantial qualifier of it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ — a warning concerning their following of conjecture and their turning away from proof.

Notice:

Al-Razi said regarding this verse:

Know that establishing the existence of the Creator by creation first, and then by guidance second, is a consistent pattern in the Qur'an. Allah, Exalted is He, related that the Friend (Khalil, Abraham), peace be upon him, mentioned this, saying: ﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 78]. And of Moses, peace be upon him, the like, when he said: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation and then guided it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 50]. And He commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) with this, saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1] ﴿who created and proportioned﴾ [al-A'la: 2] ﴿and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 3]. This is in reality a noble proof, because the human being has a body and a soul. Establishing the existence of the Creator through the states of the body is creation, and establishing it through the states of the soul is guidance. Here too, when he mentioned the proof of creation in the first verse, which is His saying: ﴿Is not He who originates creation then repeats it?﴾ [al-Naml: 64], He followed it with the proof of guidance in this verse. The purpose of creating the body is the attainment of guidance for the soul, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts that perhaps you would give thanks﴾ [al-Nahl: 78]. This is almost an explicit statement that He, Exalted is He, only created the body and only gave the senses so that they might serve as instruments for acquiring knowledge and sciences. Moreover, bodily states are base, their outcome returning to the enjoyment of tasting some flavors or touching some tangible qualities. As for spiritual states and divine knowledge, they are perfections that endure forever, preserved from coming into being and passing away. So we know that creation is subordinate to guidance, and the noblest and highest purpose is the attainment of guidance. And because of the disturbance of minds and the dispersion of thoughts, guidance and the perception of truth were by His help alone, Exalted is He. Guidance is either an expression for the call to truth, or for attaining knowledge of it, and in either case we have shown that it is the noblest of ranks and the highest of felicities, and that it is nothing but from Him, Exalted is He. As for idols, they are inanimate objects with no effect in calling to the truth nor in guiding to sincerity. Thus it is established that He, Exalted is He, is the one who conveys to all good things in this world and the next, and the guide to all perfections in soul and body, and that idols have no effect in any of that. Since this is so, their worship is pure ignorance and sheer folly. This is the summary of the discussion on this argument. End.

Then Allah, exalted is He, clarified the truth of this revealed Revelation, returning to what the surah opened with: the truthfulness of the prophethood of the one to whom it was sent down, and its proofs in the cosmic signs of Allah, which announce His great power and magnificent care in guiding His creation. So the Exalted said:

Then He clarified (p-3350) the discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿This Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from Allah, but it is a confirmation of what came before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿This Qur'an could not have been fabricated apart from Allah﴾ because that is impossible, since no one other than Him possesses the perfect power by which the inimitability (i'jaz) is general. ﴿but it is a confirmation of what came before it﴾, meaning confirming the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms regarding monotheism and the description of the Prophet ﷺ. The word (taṣdīq) is in the accusative, either as the predicate of (kāna) or as a cause for an omitted verb, i.e., He sent it down as a confirmation, etc. It was also read in the nominative as a predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., it is the confirmation of what came before it. That is, by this it is established that it is from Allah, exalted is He, because he (the Prophet) did not read them and did not sit with their people. ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, meaning a clarification of what has been prescribed and enjoined of rulings and laws, from His saying ﴿the Book of Allah upon you﴾ [an-Nisa': 24]. As 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: in it is the news of what came before you, the report of what comes after you, and the judgment between you. ﴿there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning free from doubt, originating from the Lord of the worlds. These are other predicates for what precedes them.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The context of the verse, after the prohibition of following conjecture, is to clarify what must be followed.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[38] ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful."﴾

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾ means: rather, do they say it? So "am" (or) is disjunctive (munqati'ah, "severing" the sentence), implicitly equivalent to "bal" (rather) together with the interrogative hamzah, according to the majority of scholars (al-Jumhur). The hamzah here expresses denunciation (inkar), meaning: that should not have been the case. It has also been said that it is connected (muttasilah), and its counterpart (mu'adil) is implied. That is: do they acknowledge it after We have explained its reality, or do they say it is a fabrication (iftira')? ﴿Say, "Then bring a surah like it"﴾ means: if the matter is as you claim, then bring, by way of fabrication, a surah like it in eloquence, in fine composition, and in the strength of its meaning. For you are the peers of the Arabs in language and eloquence, and more practiced in arrangement (nazm). ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful﴾ means: call upon, besides Him, Exalted is He, whomever among His creatures you are able to, to help you produce its like, if you are truthful in your claim that I invented it. For none of them is able to do so.

Abu al-Su'ud said: His exclusion of Himself, glorified is He, from the scope of the call is to make explicit their disavowal of Him, Exalted is He, and their position in the zone of opposition and hostility. It is not to explain that He alone has the power over what they were charged with. For that would give the impression that, if they had called upon Him, Exalted is He, He would have answered them in it.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿Nay, they denied that of which they had no knowledge, and its interpretation (ta'wil, the ultimate meaning or outcome) had not yet come to them. Likewise did those before them deny. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Nay, they denied that of which they had no knowledge﴾: This is a turning away from, and a transition from, demonstrating the falsehood of what they said about the Great Qur'an by challenge, to demonstrating it by explaining that their speech arises from their ignorance of its sublime matter. That is, they hastened to deny it, and they confronted it at the very first moment of hearing it, before they understood it and knew the reality of its matter, and before they reflected upon it, and came to know its interpretation and meanings, and the proofs within its folds that show it is not something a created being could produce. This was due to their extreme aversion to what contradicts their religion and their fleeing from abandoning the religion of their fathers. It is like one raised upon imitation among the Hashwiyya (a term for literalist, unreflective masses), when he senses a word that does not agree with what he was raised upon and accustomed to, even if it is brighter than the sun in the manifestation of correctness and the clarity of rectitude. He rejects it at the first instant, and recoils from it, before his hearing perceives it, without reflection on whether it is correct or corrupt; for his heart has only perceived the correctness of his own school and the corruption of all other schools. The secret of the expression ﴿that of which they had no knowledge﴾ is the indication of the completeness of their ignorance of it, and that their denial of it is only because of their not knowing it. So said al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) and Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿And its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾: That is, the explanation of what it leads to, of what He threatened them with in it. This meaning is the correct one in the verse, and more than one scholar has followed it.

In Tanwir al-Iqtibas (it is said): That is, the outcome of what He promised them in the Qur'an.

Al-Jalal (al-Mahalli) said: That is, the outcome of what it contains of threat.

Al-Qashani said: Its interpretation: that is, the manifestation of what it pointed to in its promises and its parables, of what its matter and knowledge will come back to, so they cannot deny it; for when its realities become manifest, it is not possible for anyone to deny it.

﴿Likewise did those before them deny﴾ [al-An'am: 148]: That is, the signs of the messengers, before reflecting upon their meanings.

﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾: That is, of their destruction because of their denial.

[43] ﴿And among them are those who look at you. Can you then guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾

﴿And among them are those who look at you. The discussion on the interpretation of His, Exalted is He, saying:

﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾, i.e., of the punishment, ﴿or We take you in death﴾, i.e., before that, ﴿to Us is their return﴾, i.e., We will fulfil for them what We promised them, however the situation turns, ﴿then Allah is Witness over what they do﴾, i.e., of their evil deeds.

And His, Exalted is He, saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[48] ﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [49] ﴿Say, "I possess not for myself any harm or benefit, except what God wills. For every nation is a term; when their term comes, they will not remain behind it an hour, nor will they precede it."﴾ [Yunus: 49]

﴿They say, "When is this promise?"﴾ as a way of deeming it remote and mocking it. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ means: that it will come to us. Because of what this implies, that its coming would be through the Prophet, may the blessings of God be upon him, it was said: ﴿Say, "I possess not for myself any harm or benefit"﴾ [Yunus: 49], meaning: even with that, its occurrence is nearer, so how could I possess for you (the power) to hasten the punishment upon you or bring forward the harm? This is because the context of the composition is to show his inability regarding it. As for the mention of benefit, it is to widen the scope by generalizing. The meaning is: I possess nothing at all.

﴿Except what God wills﴾ [Yunus: 49], meaning: except that I should possess it, or rather, what God wills occurs. Thus the exception is either connected (muttasil) or disconnected (munqati', i.e., not of the same kind). Abu al-Su'ud preferred the second, arguing that the first is rejected by the context of disavowing that he, peace be upon him, has any part in bringing about the promise. He elaborated his explanation.

(p-3356) Some verification scholars have stated that the exception by will has been used in the style of the Noble Qur'an to indicate permanence and continuity, as in this verse, and in His words: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾ [Hud: 107]. He said: The point of the exception is to clarify that these fixed, enduring matters are so only by the will of God, Exalted is He, not by their own nature in themselves; and had He willed to change them, He would have done so. End of quote. It is most precious, so let it be carefully memorized.

His words, Exalted is He, ﴿For every nation is a term﴾ [Yunus: 49], meaning: for every single member of every nation there is a specified term. ﴿When their term comes, they will not remain behind it an hour, nor will they precede it﴾ [Yunus: 49]. Then he hinted that the lesser resurrection is the expiration of their appointed terms with God, by His words: ﴿For every nation is a term﴾ [Yunus: 49], and so on.
