**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[62] ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [63] ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah.﴾ [Yunus: 63] [64] ﴿For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. There is no alteration to the words of Allah. That is the great attainment.﴾ [Yunus: 64]

﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah﴾: *awliyā'* is the plural of *walī*, which originally means the opposite of "enemy" and signifies "one who loves." It is permissible for it to carry here the sense of the active participle, i.e., those who take Him as their ally through obedience, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies – then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 56]. It may also carry the sense of the passive participle, i.e., the One who takes them as allies through honouring them, as in His saying: ﴿Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257], and His saying: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 55], and so on. The two meanings are mutually entailed. ﴿There is no fear concerning them﴾ of befalling something disliked. ﴿Nor will they grieve﴾, i.e., from the greatest terror, as in His saying: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103].

﴿Those who believed﴾ [Yunus: 63], i.e., in everything that came from Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And used to be mindful of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 63], i.e., they fear their Lord, so they carry out His commands and avoid His prohibitions, namely shirk, disbelief and grave sins. The position of the relative clause is in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, as if it were said: "Who are these people, and what is the cause of their attaining that honour?" It was answered: "They are those who combined faith and God-consciousness (*taqwā*), which lead to every good and save from every evil." Alternatively, it is in the accusative, governed by an omitted verb.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus: 64]. *Al-bushrā* (good tidings) is a verbal noun. It may remain as a verbal noun, with the object of the good tidings omitted, i.e., for them is the glad tiding in both of them of Paradise. It was omitted because it is known from other verses, such as His saying: ﴿Those who believed, emigrated and struggled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 20], up to His saying: ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens, for them therein is lasting pleasure﴾ [al-Tawbah: 21], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast – the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised"﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. Or it may refer to the thing given as good tidings, and its definiteness is for a known reference, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and on their right: "Good tidings for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. That is the great attainment"﴾ [al-Hadid: 12].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no alteration to the words of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 64], i.e., to His promises. ﴿That﴾ [Yunus: 64], i.e., your good tidings, which is ﴿the Garden﴾, ﴿is the great attainment﴾ [Yunus: 64], i.e., the sublime gain beyond which there is no further aim. How could it not be, when they have attained the Garden and all that is in it, and have been saved from the Fire and all that is in it?

**Admonition:**
This noble verse is a foundation for explaining the allies of Allah. Allah, in His Book, and His Messenger, in his Sunnah, have made clear that Allah has allies from among mankind, just as Satan has allies. Imam Taqi al-Din ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote a book on this titled *al-Furqan bayna Awliya' al-Rahman wa Awliya' al-Shaytan* (The Criterion between the Allies of the Merciful and the Allies of Satan). We quote from it a passage worth reflecting upon, because of how frequently the terms *walī* and *awliyā'* circulate on people's tongues. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"When one knows that among people there are allies of the Merciful and allies of Satan, one must distinguish between these and those, just as Allah and His Messenger distinguished between them. The allies of Allah are the believers who are mindful of Him, as in this verse, and in the authentic hadith narrated by al-Bukhari and others, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Allah says: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him, or I have informed him of war…' – the hadith. This is the most authentic hadith narrated about the allies, and it indicates that whoever shows enmity to an ally of Allah has openly challenged Allah to war."

In another hadith: "Indeed I avenge My allies just as the fierce lion avenges" – i.e., I take their vengeance on those who oppose them, just as the lion takes its vengeance. This is because the allies of Allah are those who believed in Him and befriended Him: they love what He loves, hate what He hates, are pleased with what He is pleased with, are angry at what He is angry at, are commanded with what He commands, are forbidden from what He forbids, give to whom He loves to give, and withhold from whom He loves to withhold.

*Wilāyah* (allegiance, friendship) is the opposite of enmity. The origin of *wilāyah* is love and nearness, and the origin of enmity is hatred and distance.

The best of the allies of Allah are His prophets. The best of His prophets are the messengers among them, and the best of them is Muhammad (ﷺ), the Seal of the Prophets and Leader of the God-conscious, whom Allah sent with the best of His books, and for whom He legislated the best of the laws of His religion, and made him the criterion distinguishing between His allies and His enemies. None is an ally of Allah except one who believes in him, in what he brought, and follows him outwardly and inwardly. Whoever claims the love and allegiance of Allah while not following him is not among the allies of Allah; rather, whoever opposes him is among the enemies of Allah and the allies of Satan. Many people think of themselves, or of others, that they are among the allies of Allah, but they are not His allies. The Jews and Christians claim that they are the allies and beloved of Allah. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Why then does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings of those He has created"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], up to the end of the verse. The polytheists of the Arabs claimed that they were the people of Allah because they dwelt in Mecca and were neighbours of the House, so He, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And they were not its allies. Its allies are only the God-conscious﴾ [al-Anfal: 34].

Just as among the disbelievers there is one who claims to be an ally of Allah while he is not an ally of Allah but rather His enemy, so too among the hypocrites who display Islam: they outwardly affirm the two testimonies of faith while inwardly believing what contradicts that. For example, they inwardly do not affirm his messengerhood, peace be upon him, and say he was merely a king obeyed, who governed people by his own opinion, of the same kind as other kings. Or they say he is the messenger only to the unlettered (Arabs) specifically. Or they say he is sent to all creation, but that Allah has specific allies to whom He did not send him and who have no need of him; rather, they have a path to Allah apart from his way, as al-Khidr had with Moses. Or they say that they take from Allah everything they need directly, benefiting from Him without an intermediary. Or they say he was sent with the outward laws, and they agree with him in these, but as for the inner realities, he was not sent with them, or he did not know them, or they know them better than he does, or they know them in the same way as one who knows them through a path other than his. All of these are disbelievers, although they believe that their own group are the allies of Allah. The allies of Allah are only those whom He described as His allies by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah﴾ [Yunus: 62–63].

Faith necessarily involves believing in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Seal of the Prophets, sent to all of mankind and jinn. Whoever does not believe in what he brought is not a believer, let alone one of the God-conscious allies of Allah. Whoever believes in some of what he brought and disbelieves in some of it is a disbeliever and not a believer.

Among faith in him is the belief that he is the intermediary between Allah and His creation in conveying His command and prohibition, His promise and threat, and His lawful and unlawful. The lawful is what Allah and His Messenger made lawful, the unlawful is what Allah and His Messenger made unlawful, and the religion is what Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) legislated. Whoever believes that any of the allies has a path to Allah apart from following Muhammad (ﷺ) is a disbeliever, one of the allies of Satan.

As for Allah's creation of creatures, His provision for them, His answering their supplications, His guidance of their hearts, His granting them victory over their enemies, and other such things of bringing benefits and repelling harms, these belong to Allah alone. He does them by whatever means He wills, and the mediation of messengers does not enter into such matters.

Furthermore, even if a man reaches the utmost in asceticism, worship and knowledge, but does not believe in all that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, he is not a believer, nor an ally of Allah, exalted is He. Such are the rabbis and monks among the scholars and worshippers of the Jews and Christians. Likewise are those who are attributed to knowledge and worship among the polytheists of the Arabs, the Turks, the Indians and others, from among the sages of India and the Turks who have knowledge, asceticism or worship in their religion, but are not believers in all that he brought. He is a disbeliever and an enemy of Allah, even if a group thinks he is an ally of Allah. Just as the sages of Persia from among the Magians were disbelieving Magians, and likewise the sages of Greece, such as Aristotle and his like, were polytheists who worshipped idols and stars. Among the categories of polytheists of these groups are some who strive in knowledge, asceticism and worship, but who are not believers in the messengers, nor do they affirm what they reported, nor obey what they commanded. These are not believers, nor allies of Allah. Such people are accompanied by devils who descend upon them, so they disclose some matters to people and have extraordinary abilities of the kind of sorcery. They are of the same kind as soothsayers and sorcerers upon whom devils descend. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying sinner. They listen eagerly, and most of them are liars﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 221–223].

All of these, who are attributed to disclosures and supernatural feats, if they are not followers of the messengers, must lie, and their devils lie to them as well. Their deeds must include something sinful and corrupt, such as some kind of shirk, injustice, grave sins, excess, or innovations in worship. For this reason the devils descended upon them and accompanied them, so they became allies of Satan, not allies of the Merciful.

Among people there is one in whom there is faith and also a trace of hypocrisy, as in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." And in Sahih Muslim: "Even if he fasts, prays, and claims that he is a Muslim."

Since the allies of Allah are the believers who are mindful of Him, the extent of a servant's allegiance to Allah, exalted is He, corresponds to the extent of his faith and God-consciousness. Whoever is more complete in faith and God-consciousness is more complete in allegiance to Allah. People differ in their allegiance to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, according to their differing levels of faith and God-consciousness, and likewise they differ in enmity toward Allah according to their differing levels of disbelief and hypocrisy.

The allies of Allah are of two classes: the foremost (*sābiqūn*) and those brought near (*muqarrabūn*), and the people of the right (*ashāb al-yamīn*) who are moderate (*muqtasidūn*). Allah mentioned them in several places in His Mighty Book. The righteous, the people of the right, are those who draw near to Allah through the obligatory duties: they do what Allah has made obligatory for them and abstain from what Allah has forbidden for them, and they do not burden themselves with recommended acts, nor with refraining from the excess of permissible things. As for the foremost, those brought near, they drew near to Him through supererogatory acts after the obligatory duties. So they performed obligations and recommended acts, and abstained from forbidden and disliked acts. When they drew near to Him through everything they were able to do of what they loved, the Lord loved them with complete love, as He said, exalted is He: "My servant continues to draw near to Me through supererogatory acts until I love him" – meaning the absolute love.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verses 62–64 (part 2 of 3):

Then, if the servant is not a friend of Allah (wali Allah) unless he is a believer and God-fearing (taqi), as this verse indicates, then it is known that none of the disbelievers or hypocrites is a friend of Allah. Likewise, one whose faith and acts of worship are not valid, even if it is supposed that he bears no sin, such as the children of disbelievers and those who have not received the call, and even if it is said that they will not be punished until a messenger is sent to them, they are not among the friends of Allah unless they are among the believers who are God-fearing. Whoever seeks nearness to Allah neither by doing good deeds nor by avoiding evil deeds is not among the friends of Allah.

Likewise, the insane and the children. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The pen is lifted from three: from the insane until he recovers, from the child until he reaches puberty, and from the sleeper until he awakens." This hadith has been related by the compilers of the Sunan from the hadith of A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), and the people of knowledge have unanimously accepted it. However, the discerning child (al-sabi al-mumayyiz) has valid acts of worship, and he is rewarded for them according to the majority of scholars. As for the insane person from whom the pen is lifted, none of his acts of worship is valid by the consensus of the scholars. Neither faith nor disbelief, neither prayer nor any other act of worship, is valid from him. Indeed, he is not fit, in the view of the general body of sensible people, for worldly affairs such as trade and crafts. He is not fit to be a cloth merchant, a perfume seller, a blacksmith or a carpenter, and his contracts are not valid by the consensus of the scholars. Thus his sale, purchase, marriage, divorce, acknowledgment and testimony are not valid, nor is any other of his statements. Rather, all his statements are nonsense (laghw), to which no legal ruling attaches, and no reward or punishment. This is unlike the discerning child (p-3371), whose statements have legal weight in certain matters by textual evidence and consensus, and in other matters there is disagreement. Since the insane person cannot be valid in faith, piety or drawing near to Allah through obligatory and voluntary acts, and it is impossible for him to be a friend of Allah, it is not permissible for anyone to believe that he is a friend of Allah, especially if his proof for that is either a revelation (mukashafa) he heard from him, or some kind of supernatural power (tasarruf), such as seeing him point at someone and that person dies or is struck down. For it is known that disbelievers and hypocrites among the polytheists and the People of the Book also have revelations and satanic powers, like soothsayers, sorcerers, and worshippers of idols and of the People of the Book. So it is not permissible for anyone to infer from such things alone that a person is a friend of Allah, if he does not know what contradicts the friendship of Allah. How much more so when he knows from him what contradicts the friendship of Allah, such as knowing that he does not believe in the obligation to follow the Prophet (ﷺ) outwardly and inwardly, but believes that he follows the outward law only and not the inner reality, or believes that the friends of Allah have a path to Allah other than the path of the prophets (peace be upon them), or says that the prophets narrowed the path, or that they are exemplars for the common people but not for the elite, and similar things that some who claim sainthood say. Such people have in them disbelief that contradicts faith, let alone the friendship of Allah, mighty and majestic. Whoever argues for their sainthood from whatever supernatural feat (kharq 'adah) proceeds from one of them is more astray than the Jews and Christians. Likewise the insane person: his being insane contradicts the validity of faith and acts of worship from him, which are conditions for the friendship of Allah. As for one who sometimes goes mad and sometimes recovers: if, in his lucid state, he is a believer in Allah and His Messenger, performs the obligatory duties and avoids what is forbidden, then when he goes mad, his madness does not prevent Allah from rewarding him for his faith and piety which he practised during his lucidity, and he has a share of Allah's friendship accordingly. Likewise, whoever becomes insane after his faith and piety, Allah rewards him and grants him reward for the faith and piety that preceded, and He does not nullify it by the madness that afflicted him without any sin of his own, and the pen is lifted from him during his madness.

Accordingly, whoever displays sainthood while he does not perform the obligatory duties and does not avoid what is forbidden, and rather does things that contradict that, no one may say: "This is a friend of Allah." For this person, if he is not insane, but is rather bewildered (mutawalliha) without madness, or his intellect is occasionally overcome by madness and occasionally recovers, and he does not carry out the obligations, but believes that it is not obligatory for him to follow the Messenger (ﷺ), then he is a disbeliever. And if he is insane both inwardly and outwardly, from whom the pen is lifted, then although he is not punished with the punishment of disbelievers, he does not deserve what believers and the God-fearing deserve of the honour of Allah, mighty and majestic. So in either case, no one may believe him to be a friend of Allah. But if he had a state in his lucidity in which he was a believer and God-fearing, he has a share of Allah's friendship accordingly. And if, in a state in which there was disbelief or hypocrisy, or if he was a disbeliever or hypocrite and then madness befell him, then he has in him the disbelief and hypocrisy for which he will be punished, and his madness does not nullify what came from him during his lucidity of disbelief or hypocrisy.

The friends of Allah have no distinguishing feature by which they stand out from people in outward matters that are permissible. They are not distinguished by one garment over another, nor by shaving the hair, trimming it or braiding it, when each of these is permissible, as it has been said: "How many a friend is in a qaba' (a cloak), and how many a heretic is in an aba' (a robe)." Rather, they are found among all the categories of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), provided they are not among the people of manifest innovation and wickedness. They are found among the people of the Qur'an, the people of knowledge, they are found among the people of jihad and the sword, they are found among the merchants, craftsmen and farmers. The early generations (al-salaf) used to call the people of religion and knowledge "the reciters" (al-qurra'), so that the scholars and the ascetics were included among them. Then after that the designations "Sufiyya" and "fuqara'" arose, and the name "Sufiyya" is attributed to the wearing of wool (suf). This is the correct view. It has been said that it is attributed to the elite of jurists (safwat al-fuqaha'), and it has been said that it is attributed to Suffa ibn Ad, a tribe of the Arabs known for asceticism, and it has been said that it is attributed to the people of the Safa, and it has been said that it is attributed to purity (safwa), and it has been said that it is attributed to the bench (suffa), and it has been said that it is attributed to the front row before Allah, exalted is He. These are weak opinions, for if it were so, it would be said "Siffi" or "Safa'i" or "Suffi," not "Sufi." The designation "fuqara'" has also come to refer to those who follow the spiritual path (ahl al-suluk), and this is a newly established usage. People have disputed which is better: the designation "Sufi" (p-3373) or the designation "faqir"? They also dispute which is better: the wealthy grateful one, or the poor patient one? The correct view in all of this is what the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13]. In the Sahih, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked: "Who among the people is best?" He said: "The most righteous of them." So the Book and the Sunna indicate that the most honoured of people in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of them. In the Sunan, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "No Arab has any merit over a non-Arab, nor a non-Arab over an Arab, nor a black person over a white person, nor a white person over a black person, except by piety." And from him (ﷺ) also: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, has removed from you the arrogance of the Jahiliyya and its pride in ancestors. People are of two kinds: a believing God-fearing one, and a wicked wretched one."

It is not a condition for a friend of Allah that he be infallible, never erring or making mistakes. Rather, it is permissible that some knowledge of the Sharia be hidden from him, and it is permissible that some matters of religion be confused for him, so that he may consider some things commanded by Allah to be among what Allah has forbidden, and it is permissible that he may suppose some supernatural occurrences to be among the miracles (karamat) of the friends of Allah, the Exalted, while they are actually from Satan, who has deceived him because of the deficiency of his rank, and he does not realise that they are from Satan. Yet this does not take him out of the friendship of Allah, the Exalted. For Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has pardoned this community for error, forgetfulness (p-3374) and what they have been compelled to do. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not hold the mujtahid who errs to be sinful; rather, he made for him a reward for his effort, and made his error forgiven. For this reason, since the friend of Allah may err, it is not obligatory upon people to believe everything that one who is a friend of Allah says, unless he is a prophet. Indeed, it is not permissible for a friend of Allah to rely upon what is cast into his heart, unless it accords with the Sharia, nor upon what befalls him of what he sees as inspiration (ilham), conversation or address from the Truth. Rather, he must present all of that to what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought. If it agrees with it, he accepts it; if it contradicts it, he does not accept it. If he does not know whether it agrees or disagrees, he withholds judgment on it.

People in this matter are of three categories: two extremes and a middle. Among them are those who, when they believe that a person is a friend of Allah, agree with him in everything they think their heart has told them from their Lord, and surrender to him all that he does. And among them are those who, when they see him say or do something that does not accord with the Sharia, expel him entirely from the friendship of Allah, even if he is a mujtahid who has erred. The best of matters is their middle course, which is that he is not made infallible nor sinful when he is a mujtahid who errs. He is not followed in everything he says, nor is he judged as a disbeliever or a transgressor for his ijtihad. The obligation upon people is to follow what Allah sent His Messenger with. As for when someone opposes the opinion of some jurists and agrees with the opinion of others, no one may compel him to follow the opinion of the one who opposes him, saying: "This has contradicted the Sharia."

In the two Sahihs, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "There used to be muhaddathun (inspired ones) among the nations before you, and if there is one in my community, it is 'Umar." 'Umar used to say: "Come close to the mouths of the obedient ones, and listen to what they say, for clear matters will be disclosed to them." The muhaddath who takes things from his heart is not infallible, so he needs to present it to what the infallible Prophet (ﷺ) brought. For this reason 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to consult the Companions, debate with them, and return to them on some matters, and they would dispute with him on things, and he would argue against them, and they would argue against him with the Book and the Sunna, and he would confirm them in their disputing with him, and he would not say to them: "I am a muhaddath, inspired, addressed, so it is incumbent upon you to accept from me and not oppose me." Whoever his companions claim is a friend of Allah, and that he is addressed, and that it is obligatory for his followers to accept from him everything he says, not to oppose him, and to submit to his state without reference to the Book and the Sunna, then he and they are in error. Such a person misguides people. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) is better than him, and he was the Commander of the Believers, and the Muslims used to dispute with him and present their objections to what he said, both he and they being upon the Book and the Sunna. The early generations of the community and its imams have agreed that everyone's words may be taken or rejected, except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this is one of the differences between the prophets and others. For this reason al-Junayd said: "This knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunna." Abu 'Uthman al-Naysaburi said: "Whoever makes the Sunna govern himself in word and deed speaks with wisdom, and whoever makes his desire govern himself in word and deed speaks with innovation," in accordance with the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ [al-Nur: 54]. And Abu 'Amr ibn Nujayd said: "Every spiritual state (wajd) that is not witnessed to by the Book and the Sunna is false."

Therefore, the friends of God (awliya' Allah) are recognized by their qualities, actions, and states, which the Book and the Sunnah indicate. They are known by the light of faith and the Qur'an, by the inner realities of faith, and by the laws of Islam (shara'i' al-Islam). So if a person is engaged in impurities and filth that Satan loves, or frequents bathhouses and latrines, where devils gather, or eats snakes, scorpions, wasps, and dogs' ears, which are filthy and harmful creatures, or drinks urine and similar impurities that Satan loves; or if he calls upon other than God, seeking help from created beings and turning toward them, or prostrates toward the direction of his shaykh and does not devote the religion sincerely to the Lord of the worlds; or if he associates with dogs or fires, or frequents garbage heaps and unclean places, or frequents graves, especially the graves of disbelievers among the Jews, Christians, or polytheists; or if he dislikes hearing the Qur'an and shrinks from it, preferring the hearing of songs and poetry, and favoring the hearing of the flutes of Satan over the speech of the Most Merciful, then these are the signs of the friends of Satan, not the signs of the friends of the Most Merciful. [Ended, summarized.]

[p-3376] The book is one that must be consulted and read word for word, for it contains benefits found nowhere else. May God have mercy on its compiler and reward him well. And His Exalted saying:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[65] ﴿And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all might belongs to Allah; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all might belongs to Allah; He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ This is a consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding what he would hear of their plotting to bring harm upon him, their openly denying him, and their accusing him of sorcery and the like. That is: do not be affected by their words, and witness the might and dominance of Allah, so that you look upon them with the gaze of annihilation (fana') and see their deeds and their words, and what they threaten you with, as dust scattered in the air. Whoever witnesses the power and might of Allah sees all power and might belonging to Him; there is no power and no strength except through Him.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, all might belongs to Allah﴾, is a justification for the prohibition, in the manner of a resumptive clause (isti'naf), as if it were said: "Why should I not grieve?" So it is said: "Indeed, all might belongs to Allah," that is, victory and dominance in His dominion and authority; none possesses any of it at all, neither they nor others. So He overcomes them and gives you victory over them: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], ﴿Indeed, We surely help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51]. And His saying ﴿He is the All-Hearing﴾, that is, of their words about you, so He will recompense them; ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, that is, of what ought to be done to them.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[66] ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah as partners do not follow [in truth] partners. They follow only assumption, and they are only guessing.﴾

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth﴾ means: all of them are under His dominion (malakah), His disposal (tasarruf), and His dominance (qahr). They have power over nothing except by His permission, His will, and His empowering them.

His saying ﴿And those who invoke other than Allah as partners do not follow [in truth] partners. They follow only assumption, and they are only guessing﴾ is a confirmation of what preceded concerning the exclusivity of might to Him, exalted is He, so that His solace (ﷺ) may increase, and it is a proof of the falsehood of their conjectures and of the statements built upon them.

In the particle (مَا, ma) in His saying ﴿وما يَتَّبِعُ﴾ (wa-ma yattabi'u), there are two possibilities:

The first: it is a negation particle, and (شُرَكاءَ, shuraka') is the object (maf'ul) of (يَتَّبِعُ, yattabi'u), and the object of (يَدْعُونَ, yad'una) is omitted because it is evident. That is: they do not follow partners, [true] partners in reality, even though they name them partners out of their ignorance. He mentioned only one of the two objects because its indication of the other is clear. It is also permissible for (شُرَكاءَ) to be the object of (يَدْعُونَ), with the object of (يَتَّبِعُ) omitted because it is understood from His saying ﴿إنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إلا الظَّنَّ﴾, meaning: they do not follow certainty; they only follow their false assumption.

The second: it is an interrogative particle (اسْتِفْهامِيَّةٌ, istifhamiyyah), in the accusative governed by (يَتَّبِعُ), and (شُرَكاءَ) is the object of (يَدْعُونَ). That is: "What is it that these people follow?" In other words, since all are under His subjugation and dominion, what they follow apart from Allah is nothing, has no effect, and no power. They only follow what they imagine in their assumptions and fancy in their imaginations, and they are only estimating the existence of something that has no existence in reality.

Then, exalted is He, drew attention to His being singular in complete power and all-encompassing blessing, so as to indicate His unity, glorified is He, in deserving worship, by His saying:

The discussion of the Words of His Exalted Saying:

[67] ﴿He it is Who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by.﴾ Indeed in that are signs for a people who hear.

﴿He it is Who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾ That is, He created it for you so that you may settle in it from your fatigue and exhaustion. ﴿And the day as something to see by﴾ That is, bright, in which you see the means of seeking your provision and your gains.

It has been said: the verse is of the type of ihtibak (ihtibak, a rhetorical device in which something mentioned in one part is omitted from the other, and vice versa). The intended sense is: He made the night dark so that you may rest in it, and the day bright so that you may move about in it for your interests; thus from each of the two parts there has been omitted what was mentioned in the other, being sufficed by what is mentioned over what is left out. The attribution of seeing (ibsar) to the day is metaphorical (majazi), like his saying:

"The night of the lover does not sleep."

﴿Indeed in that﴾ That is, the making mentioned ﴿are signs for a people who hear﴾ That is, these signs and their like, hearing with contemplation and reflection.

Then he proceeded to another kind of their falsehoods with His Exalted Saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[68] ﴿They say: "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. You have no authority (*sultan*, here meaning proof or evidence) for this. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾

﴿They say: "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him!﴾ This is a declaration that He is exalted above resembling anyone or needing anyone, and an expression of wonder at their foolish statement. ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient﴾, meaning the One whose existence is by His own essence and through whom the existence of everything exists. How then could anything be like Him? And how could anything be of His kind, when all existence belongs to Him? This clause gives the reason for His being declared exalted above that, and indicates that taking a son is among the attributes of need, either to gain strength through him or to preserve one's kind. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ affirms His self-sufficiency: since He possesses them, He is independent of taking any of them as a son. ﴿You have no authority for this﴾, meaning you have no proof for this false statement. This clarifies its falsehood, since the clear demonstration that has been established is free from opposition. That is, there is no proof after this that could be heard. The purpose is to show their ignorance, and that they have no basis except the blind imitation (*taqlid*) of their predecessors and the following of one ignorant person by another.

Note:

The verse indicates that proof is called *sultan*.

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah*: Indeed, He, glory be to Him, named the rational proof a *sultan*. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Every *sultan* in the Qur'an is a proof." This is like His saying, exalted is He, ﴿You have no authority for this﴾, meaning: you have no proof for what you have said; it is nothing but speaking about Allah without knowledge. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿These are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [al-Najm: 23] (p. 3379), meaning He has sent down for them no proof or evidence, but they are from your own inventions and those of your fathers. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾ [al-Saffat: 156], meaning clear proof. There is only one place where this has been disputed, which is His saying: ﴿My wealth has not availed me﴾ [al-Haqqah: 28] ﴿My authority has perished from me﴾ [al-Haqqah: 29]. It was said that what is meant here is power and dominion, that is, my wealth and my kingdom have gone from me, so I have neither wealth nor authority. It was also said that it retains its original meaning, that is, my proof has been cut off and nullified, so I have no proof. The point is that Allah, glory be to Him, named the knowledge of proof a *sultan*, because it necessitates the authority and power of its holder. Thus he has, through it, a *sultan* over the ignorant. Indeed, the authority of knowledge is greater than the authority of the hand. For this reason people submit to proof more than they submit to the hand, since hearts submit to proof, whereas the hand only subdues the body. Proof captures the heart and leads it, and humbles the opponent, even if he displays obstinacy and arrogance; his heart is submissive to it, humbled and subdued under its authority. Moreover, the authority of position, if it is not accompanied by knowledge by which it is governed, is like the authority of beasts of prey, lions and the like: power without knowledge or mercy. Unlike the authority of proof, which is power with knowledge, mercy and wisdom. Whoever does not have power through his knowledge is either due to the weakness of his proof and authority, or due to the coercion of the authority of the hand and the sword over him. Otherwise, proof supports itself, and prevails over falsehood, overcoming it. (End of quotation.)

﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ This is a rebuke and reproach for their ignorance. Al-Zamakhshari said: When He denied them proof, He made them people who do not know. This indicates that every statement for which its speaker has no proof is ignorance and not knowledge.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In this there is a warning that every assertion for which there is no evidence is ignorance, that beliefs must have a definitive proof, and that blind imitation is far from being considered valid.

The commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[69] ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed.﴾ [70] ﴿(They have) an enjoyment in this world; then to Us will be their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ [Yunus: 70]

﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah﴾ by ascribing offspring to Him and associating partners with Him, ﴿will not succeed﴾, meaning they will not attain, at all, the thing sought. ﴿(They have) an enjoyment in this world﴾ [Yunus: 70] is a mubtada' (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e., for them there is a brief enjoyment in the world. ﴿Then to Us will be their return﴾ [Yunus: 70], i.e., through death. ﴿Then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 70], i.e., because of their disbelief. The verse serves to explain that what appears as their success in worldly portions is far removed from being a kind of success (falah). It is as if it were said: How will they not succeed while they are in prosperity and bliss? So it is said: it is a brief enjoyment in the world, and it is not an attainment of the sought-after thing.
