And His words, exalted is He:

The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:

[71] ﴿And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has been burdensome to you, then upon Allah I have relied. So resolve upon your affair, along with your partners, then let not your affair be obscure to you; then carry it out against me and do not give me respite."﴾

﴿And recite to them the news of Noah﴾ i.e., his account, which is of great significance and weight, [related] with his people who were deceived by the power of wealth and helpers, so that they may reflect upon what it contains of the soundness of his reliance upon Allah, and his regard for his people with the eye of not caring about them or their schemes, and the vanishing of what they enjoyed of blessings through their drowning by the flood. Perhaps they would then desist from their disbelief, their hearts would soften, and they would become certain of the truth of your prophethood ﴿when he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing [among you] has been burdensome to you"﴾, i.e., has been difficult and heavy. ﴿My standing﴾, i.e., my place, meaning himself; or my long remaining among you, for a span of a thousand years less fifty years; or my standing in calling to Allah, [which is burdensome] because of your seeing my lowliness through the scarcity of wealth and helpers, and your preventing [me] by them from submitting to me. ﴿And my reminding you of the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., of His proofs and evidences, or my warning you of His punishment. ﴿Then upon Allah I have relied﴾, i.e., I have depended, in repelling what you intend against me with it. ﴿So resolve upon your affair﴾, i.e., your matter concerning my destruction. ﴿along with your partners﴾, meaning their gods, and this is mockery of them; or their counterparts in polytheism. The "waw" [in "wa shurakaakum"] is in the sense of "with", or it is coordinated with "amrakum" by omitting the genitive-governed noun, i.e., "and the affair of your partners"; or it is in the accusative governed by an omitted verb, i.e., "call upon your partners." That is because (ajma'a) relates to meanings, as it is said: "ajma'a al-amr" when he intended it and resolved upon it. ﴿Then let not your affair be obscure to you﴾, i.e., concealed, from (ghamma-hu, when he covered it), but rather openly manifest, which you declare to me. ﴿Then carry it out against me﴾, i.e., deliver to me that matter which you intend against me. ﴿And do not give me respite﴾, i.e., do not delay me.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[72] ﴿And if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among those who submit.﴾

﴿And if you turn away﴾, i.e., from belief in what I have brought you. ﴿Then I have not asked you for any reward﴾, i.e., any wage (ju'l) for my admonition to you, meaning there is no motive left for you to turn away and recoil. ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, i.e., my recompense for the reminder is only from Him, exalted is He, who rewards me for it, whether you believe or turn away. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among those who submit﴾, i.e., those who surrender to Him alone by believing in Him and rejecting every object of worship besides Him.

"The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:"

[73] ﴿But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We made them successors, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. So look at how was the end of those who were warned.﴾

﴿But they denied him﴾ meaning Noah, with what he brought them, out of obstinacy, after the proof had been established against them, so the word of punishment was due against them, and He sent upon them the flood. ﴿So We saved him﴾, that is, from drowning, ﴿and those with him in the ship﴾ ﴿and We made them successors﴾, that is, successors in place of those who were drowned, and inhabitants of the earth. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. So look at how was the end of those who were warned﴾, that is, the final outcome of their affair. What is meant by "those who were warned" is "the deniers." The use of this expression is an indication of their persistence in it, since the warning had no effect upon them. It is part of the divine custom that a people is not destroyed by total annihilation except after warning, for whoever has been warned has been given an excuse. In the command to look there is both an emphasis on the magnitude of what befell them and a warning to whoever denies the Messenger (ﷺ), and a consolation for him.

The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:

[74] ﴿Then after him We sent messengers to their peoples, and they brought them clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors.﴾

﴿Then after him﴾ means: after Noah. ﴿Messengers to their peoples﴾ refers to Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot and Shu'ayb. ﴿And they brought them clear proofs﴾ means the signs that point to their truthfulness and that yield their guidance. ﴿But they were not going to believe in what they had denied before﴾ means: because of their habituation to denying the truth and their training in it, for before the sending of the messengers they were a people of ignorance (jahiliyyah), denying the truth, so their condition after them was like their condition before them. This is on the reading that the pronoun in (kanu) and (kadhdhabu) refers to the peoples of the messengers. It is also permissible for the pronoun in (kanu) to refer to the peoples of the messengers and the pronoun in (kadhdhabu) to refer to the people of Noah, meaning: the people of the messengers were not going to believe in what the people of Noah had denied, that is, in its like. ﴿Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾ means: those who exceed the requirements of the realities of things, by His forsaking them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 75:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[75] ﴿Then, after them, We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they acted arrogantly, and they were a criminal people.﴾

﴿Then, after them⁠﴾ means: after these messengers. ﴿Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs⁠﴾ means: the nine (signs). ﴿But they acted arrogantly, and they were a criminal people⁠﴾ means: they were disbelievers possessing great sins.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[76] ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is clear magic."﴾

﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾ means the signs that remove doubt. ﴿They said﴾ means, out of extreme rebelliousness. ﴿Indeed, this is clear magic﴾ means manifest deception.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 10, Verse 77:**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:**

[77] ﴿Moses said, "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' And magicians do not succeed."﴾

﴿Moses said, "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you"﴾: that is, in a manner that leaves you no doubt. Your foolish statement, that it is magic, has been omitted, and the thing said (al-mahkiy al-maqul) is left out because the context points to it. Then he said, ﴿Is this magic?﴾ This is an interrogative of denial (istifham inkar) spoken by Moses, not by them. It is a new clause (mustani'if) that denies that it is magic, refutes their claim, and rebukes them for it after an earlier rebuke. ﴿Is this magic?﴾ is not their own statement, because they had already firmly asserted that it was magic, so how could they ask about it? This is what has been said.

I see no barrier to it being their own statement. The hamza (interrogative particle) is placed in the middle as an extra element (mazidah) to strengthen the interrogation before it. One of its subtleties is to guard against the impression that magic was the agent of ﴿has come to you﴾ from the outset. The style of the Qur'an is above every style. Alternatively, the hamza and what follows it are part of their first statement, when they were surprised by the miracle of Moses. Their earlier statement, ﴿Indeed, this is clearly magic﴾ [Yunus: 76], is a report of the statement by which they had settled their position. Later I saw that al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munir) in al-Intisaf pointed to this when he said:

As for the second reading, that is the reading of "a-al-sihr" (ءالسِّحْرُ) in the interrogative form, it contains, and God knows best, a guidance that the words of Moses at first, ﴿Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, "Is this magic?"﴾, are a report of their statement, and that ﴿Is this magic?﴾ is what they said. God's report about them, that they said ﴿Indeed, this is clearly magic﴾ [Yunus: 76], does not contradict this. That is either because they said both things: they began with the interrogative, in the manner of scorning the truth and mocking that it is the truth, and mockery of the truth is a denial of it. Indeed, in some contexts the interrogative can be more emphatic in its affirmation than a declarative. Do you not see that they say, in the line of poetry, "Are you Umm Salim?" (أأنْتِ أُمُّ سالِمٍ), which is more emphatic in its affirmation than saying, reporting it: "You are Umm Salim." Then they repeated it with the declarative form, which is specific to the emphatic affirmation of denial and of the claim that it is magic, saying ﴿Indeed, this is clearly magic﴾ [Yunus: 76]. So God, exalted is He, reported this second statement, and Moses rebuked them for their first statement. The meanings of the two expressions and their outcome are one. Or, they said nothing but ﴿Is this magic?﴾ in the manner of denial as mentioned above, and God reported it by its outcome, because He knows that their intention by the interrogative was denial and the firm assertion that it was magic. Moses, peace be upon him, reported their statement in its own words and did not render it in other words.

The reporting of the narratives recited in the Mighty Book in various forms has no explanation except that they are meanings transmitted into the Arabic language, so they are rendered by synonymous words of equal meaning.

The conclusion of this discussion is that the words of Moses, peace be upon him, ﴿Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, "Is this magic?"﴾, report their statement. What points to this is that when they brought magic he answered them with a similar statement in the interrogative form, saying, "What you have brought, is it magic?" (ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ آالسِّحْرُ) (according to the reading with the interrogative), an exchange of like for like. What confirms for you that the interrogative and the declarative have one and the same meaning in such a sense is that God, exalted is He, reported the words of Moses, peace be upon him, ﴿What you have brought is magic﴾ [Yunus: 81], in both forms, the declarative and the interrogative, as the two readings require, and it is one statement. This shows that the import of the two is one, since the declarative is necessarily true.

What led al-Zamakhshari to interpret "say" (al-qawl) as "blame" (al-ta'yib) or to posit an omitted object for "you say" (taqulun) was the difficulty of an interrogative being reported by a verb of saying while what is reported of them is a declarative. We have made clear that there is neither incongruity nor contradiction between the two matters.

Al-Nasir said: "By this section he has strengthened the bonds of this argument, for it is among the finest subtleties. And God is the Granter of success."

(p-3385) As for His words, the Exalted, ﴿And magicians do not succeed﴾, these are certainly the words of Moses. He said them to affirm what preceded, because when the truth being magic entails that the one who brought it is a magician, he reinforced the earlier denial and the rebuke and ignorance contained in it by this statement.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[78] ﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers, and so that you two may have greatness in the land? We will not believe you two."﴾

﴿They said﴾, i.e., to Musa (Moses), ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away"﴾, i.e., to divert us, ﴿"from that upon which we found our fathers"﴾, meaning the worship of idols, ﴿"and so that you two may have greatness"﴾, i.e., kingship and authority, ﴿"in the land"﴾, i.e., the land of Egypt, ﴿"We will not believe you two"﴾, i.e., so that our might may remain.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 79:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[79] ﴿And Pharaoh said, "Bring me every learned sorcerer."﴾

﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, i.e., to preserve his dignity and to repel the rising prestige of Moses, ﴿"Bring me every learned sorcerer"﴾, i.e., one skilled in his craft.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[80] ﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down whatever you are going to throw."﴾

﴿So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, "Throw down whatever you are going to throw."﴾ That is, of the kinds of magic. Some of them said: it is permissible to order the performance of magic in order to refute it, and likewise to request that doubts be presented so that they may be resolved.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[81] ﴿So when they had cast, Moses said: "What you have brought is sorcery. Indeed, Allah will render it void. Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of the corrupters to prosper."﴾

﴿So when they had cast﴾ — that is, their staffs and ropes, in order to imitate the miracle of Moses with his staff. ﴿Moses said (p-3386): "What you have brought is sorcery"﴾ — that is, it is sorcery, not what I have brought to you, which you have called sorcery. ﴿Indeed, Allah will render it void﴾ — that is, He will utterly obliterate it by means of my miracle, so that no trace of it remains. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of the corrupters to prosper﴾ — that is, rather He will bring ruin upon it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[82] ﴿And Allah establishes the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.﴾

﴿And Allah establishes the truth by His words﴾ — i.e., He makes it firm and strengthens it by them. ﴿Even if the criminals dislike it﴾ — i.e., that. And His words, exalted is He:

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[83] ﴿But none believed in Moses except some of his people's descendants, out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would persecute them. Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land, and indeed he was among the extravagant.﴾

﴿But none believed in Moses except some of his people's descendants﴾ is conjoined (ma'tuf) to a known implied clause found in other places, meaning: ﴿So Moses cast down his staff, and behold, it swallowed up what they had falsely fabricated﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 45], and so on. It has been said: the pronoun in ﴿his people﴾ refers to Pharaoh, and they were a small group from his people who believed in him secretly. The more evident view is that they were the people of Moses, namely the Children of Israel (Bani Isra'il), who were in Egypt, the descendants of Ya'qub (Jacob). They are the ones who believed in him ﴿out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would persecute them﴾, i.e., that he would torment them. ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh was haughty﴾, i.e., arrogant, ﴿in the land﴾, i.e., the land of Egypt, ﴿and indeed he was among the extravagant﴾, i.e., those who exceed the limit through injustice and corruption, and through claiming lordship.

**Verse 84: The Commentary on His Words, Exalted is He**

﴿And Moses said, "O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims."﴾

﴿And Moses said﴾, meaning: to calm their hearts and to remove fear from them. ﴿"O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him"﴾, meaning: so entrust your affairs to Him for protection from what you fear, and place your trust in Him, for He is sufficient for you. ﴿"Whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him"﴾ (65:3). His words ﴿"if you are Muslims"﴾ mean: sincerely devoting your faces to Him.

Al-Qashani said: He made tawakkul (reliance on God) a necessary consequence of Islam, which is the submission of the face to God Most High. That is, if your faith and certainty are perfected, such that they have an effect on your souls and make them sincere to God, then reliance upon Him becomes necessary. If "Islam" is taken in the sense of submission and compliance, then it is a condition for tawakkul, not something it necessarily entails. In that case its meaning is: if your faith is sound and certain, then rely upon Him, on condition that you are submitting. It is like saying: "If you dislike this tree, then uproot it, if you are able." End of quotation.

Al-Karkhi said: His words ﴿"if you are Muslims"﴾ mean: submitting to His command. So His words ﴿"then rely upon Him"﴾ are the answer to the first condition, and the second condition, ﴿"if you are Muslims"﴾, is a condition attached to the first. This is because when two conditions are not arranged in sequence in existence, the second condition is a condition upon the first. For this reason it was not necessary to place it before the first. The jurists said: "The latter must be treated as earlier, and the earlier as later." An example of this is a man's saying to his wife: "If you enter the house, then you are divorced, if you speak to Zayd." So the whole statement "If you enter the house, then you are divorced" is conditioned by his words "if you speak to Zayd." The conditioned clause comes after the condition, and this requires that what comes later in wording be earlier in meaning, and what comes earlier in wording be later in meaning. It is as if he is saying to his wife: "At the time you speak to Zayd, if you enter the house, then you are divorced." So if this conditioned matter occurred before she spoke to Zayd, the divorce would not take effect.

Thus His words, exalted is He, ﴿"if you have believed"﴾ and so on, require that their being Muslims be a condition for them to become addressed by His words ﴿"if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him"﴾. It is as if He, exalted is He, is saying to the Muslim at the time of his submission: "If you are among those who believe in God, then rely upon God." The matter is indeed so, because Islam is an expression of surrender (al-istislam), which is compliance with God's obligations and abandoning rebellion, while faith (iman) is an expression of the heart's knowledge that the Necessary Existent in Himself is One, and that everything else is originated, under His management and subjugation. When these two states are realized, the servant then entrusts all his affairs to God Most High, and the light of reliance upon God arises in the heart. End of quotation.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[85] ﴿So they said, "In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.﴾

﴿So they said, "In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people.﴾ That is, a place of trial (fitnah) for them, meaning a punishment by which they would torment us and tempt us away from our religion. Al-Hakim said: It indicates the goodness of asking for deliverance from the oppressors.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[86] ﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.﴾

﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.﴾ That is: from their scheming, and from the ill omen of seeing them, and from being enslaved to them.

Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: In placing reliance upon God (tawakkul) before supplication (du'a'), there is an admonition that the one who supplicates should first place his reliance upon God, so that his supplication may be answered.

The discussion of the Lord's words:

[87] ﴿And We revealed to Moses and his brother: "Settle your people in Egypt in houses, and make your houses a qiblah, and establish the prayer, and give good tidings to the believers."﴾

﴿And We revealed to Moses and his brother: "Settle your people in Egypt in houses"﴾ That is, take for yourselves in it houses as dwelling-places (mubā'ah) in which you remain constantly, so that your word (kalimah) concerning your affair may be united. ﴿"And make your houses a qiblah"﴾ That is, a place of prayer (muṣallā). ﴿"And establish the prayer"﴾ That is, in your houses. Some of them said: they were fearful, and in this there is an indication of the permissibility of concealing the prayer at the time of fear. ﴿"And give good tidings to the believers"﴾ That is, of victory in this world, and of Paradise in the next.

(p-٣٣٨٩) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[88] ﴿And Moses said: "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the worldly life. Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."﴾

﴿And Moses said﴾, meaning he was calling upon God, exalted is He, to remove the might of Pharaoh. ﴿Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment﴾, meaning what they adorn themselves with of clothing, mounts, and jewelry. ﴿And wealth in the worldly life. Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way﴾, meaning through arrogance toward You, Your signs, and Your messengers. His saying "that they may lead astray" (liyuḍillū) is connected to "You have given" (ātayta), and "Our Lord" is repeated for emphasis. The "lām" in "liyuḍillū" is the lām of consequence and outcome (lām al-ʿāqibah, the "lām" indicating the result that follows). That is: You gave them the aforementioned blessings so that they would be grateful and follow Your way, but the outcome of their affair was that they disbelieved and strayed from Your way. Permitting the "lām" to be a lām of purpose is a gradual leading (istidrāj, God's gradual drawing of a person into punishment), or a lām of supplication against them for that reason. This is an extravagance beyond what the context allows, and a turning away from the gentleness and the secret of the context. When Moses saw the people persisting in disbelief and obstinacy, he began to supplicate against them. It is proper for one who calls down a curse upon others to first present what prompted his supplication and compelled him to entreat, so that his supplication may be answered. Therefore, he first made clear their straying from the way through their ingratitude for the blessings and their defiance toward the one who bestowed them, as a preface to his saying: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾, meaning destroy it, because they use Your blessing to aid their disobedience to You. The root of "obliteration" (al-ṭams) is the erasing of a trace and altering. ﴿And harden their hearts﴾, meaning make them hard, and seal them, so that they do not open to faith. ﴿So they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾, meaning they will witness it and be certain of it, in such a way that this will not benefit them at that time. His saying ﴿so they will not believe﴾ is either the answer to the supplication or a supplication expressed in the form of a prohibition.

Ibn Kathir said: This supplication from Moses, peace be upon him, was out of anger for God and His religion against Pharaoh and his chiefs, who had become clear to him as people in whom there is no good and from whom nothing will come. Just as Noah, peace be upon him, supplicated, saying: (p-٣٣٩٠) ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾ [Nuh: 26] ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾ [Nuh: 27]. For this reason, God, exalted is He, answered Moses regarding them with this supplication, in which his brother Harun joined him, as He informed us by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[89] ﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered, so go straight and do not follow the way of those who do not know."﴾

﴿He said﴾ (exalted is He): ﴿Your supplication has been answered, so go straight﴾, i.e., adhere to My command, and do not be hasty, for what you seek will certainly occur in its time without doubt. ﴿And do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾, i.e., in haste, or in not being certain of His promise, exalted is He. Or it refers to Pharaoh and his people, by His words, glorified is He.

Then, exalted is He, pointed to the answering of their supplication concerning the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[90] ﴿And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers followed them in wrongdoing and enmity, until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾

﴿And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers followed them﴾, i.e., overtook them. ﴿In wrongdoing and enmity﴾, i.e., for the sake of oppressing them and transgressing against them. ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said﴾, hoping to be saved from drowning: ﴿"I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾

The reason is that when Musa (peace be upon him) asked Fir'awn (Pharaoh) to release the Israelites from their servitude and to permit them to depart to Filastin (Palestine) to worship their Lord, he refused and rebelled. So Allah struck him and his people with the nine signs, as has preceded in the surah al-A'raf [p-3391]. He then permitted Musa and his people to leave Misr (Egypt). The Children of Israel set out all together with their livestock and belongings. Then Fir'awn and his chiefs regretted releasing them from their service, so Fir'awn and his soldiers pressed on in their pursuit to bring them back. They overtook them while they were camped by the sea. The Israelites feared his approach and cried out to Musa, so he calmed their fears and informed them of what they would witness of their own deliverance and the destruction of their enemy. Allah, exalted is He, revealed to Musa that he should strike the sea with his staff, and it split. The Children of Israel entered into its midst upon the dry path which Allah, exalted is He, had made a great sign, and they passed through it to its far shore. Fir'awn and his soldiers followed them, until, when they had reached the middle of the sea, Musa extended his hand over the sea, and it returned to what it had been. Fir'awn drowned along with those who were with him.

When he sensed the drowning, he sought refuge in faith, seeking deliverance, and it was said to him:

Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted:

[91] ﴿Now? And you had already disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters.﴾

﴿Now?﴾ That is, will you now believe and submit, so that you may be saved from drowning? ﴿And you had already disobeyed before﴾ That is, you disbelieved in Allah before the drowning. ﴿And you were among the corrupters﴾ That is, through misguidance and leading others astray, and through wrongdoing and arrogant rebellion.

[p-3392] **Note:**

Al-Shihab al-Khafaji said in *al-'Inayah*: A person's faith is not accepted at the moment of despair and death (*ihtidar*), as the explicit text of the verse indicates: ﴿Then their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 85]. As for what appears in *al-Fusus* about the validity of his faith, and that His saying ﴿the Children of Israel believed in Him﴾ [Yunus: 90] refers to faith in Musa (peace be upon him), this contradicts the text and the *ijma'* (scholarly consensus). Al-Jalal al-Dawani, may Allah have mercy on him, did take its apparent meaning. He has a treatise on this, which I have read, and I was amazed by it until I saw in *Tarikh Halab* by al-Fadil al-Halabi that it is not his, but belongs to a man called Muhammad ibn Hilal al-Nahwi. Al-Qazwini refuted it and condemned it, saying: His example is that of a man of obscure reputation who, when he came to Makkah, urinated in Zamzam so that he would become famous among people, as in the proverb "Oppose and you will be known." In *Fatawa Ibn Hajar*, may Allah have mercy on him, it is stated that some of our jurists declared disbelievers those who held that Pharaoh had believed. For this reason it has been said that by "Pharaoh" in his speech is meant the commanding soul (*al-nafs al-ammara*). All of this is unnecessary. End of al-Shihab's words.

I say: Our shaykh al-'Attar, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his book *al-Fath al-Mubin fi Radd I'tiraD al-Mu'tarid 'ala Muhyi al-Din* a concluding section on the falsehood of what is attributed to this gnostic (*'arif*) regarding the validity of Pharaoh's faith and his salvation. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Let it be known that it has spread among the people of knowledge that His Eminence Muhyi al-Din, may Allah be pleased with him, said that Pharaoh believed and was saved, whereas the reality is not so, as you will see from the quotations from him. Yes, he examined the question of the validity or invalidity of the claim that Pharaoh believed and was saved, based on the Qur'anic verses. This was, on his part, merely an examination of the evidence and nothing more. It was not a definitive statement that he believed. He built the issue of Pharaoh's salvation and faith on two of his principles, on which a great multitude of eminent scholars agreed with him.

The first principle: in clarifying the reality of the faith of despair (*iman al-yas*). According to him, and according to a great multitude of scholars, it is the faith that occurs at the sight of the punishment of the barzakh (intermediate state), like the condition of the dying person only. At this state faith does not benefit, and this is agreed upon among the people of knowledge. Some people held that the faith of despair is that which occurs at the sight of punishment, whether worldly or otherworldly, so faith in either state does not benefit. According to this gnostic and a group of scholars, the sight of worldly punishment does not prevent the validity of faith, even though it necessitates destruction in this world. Allah's sunnah (way) decrees that the worldly destruction is inevitable for one who sees this punishment, even if he believes and is saved from the punishment of the Hereafter, except the people of Yunus, for He, may He be exalted, saved them from it, as He mentioned.

The second of his principles, may Allah be pleased with him: whoever has had the Word decreed against him does not utter the substance of faith intending faith, and even if he utters it, he does not intend it. So Allah, may He be exalted, must refute him, even if only by narrating about him, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils they say, "We are with you"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14], and as He said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. Thus He refuted their claim. This principle is derived from His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe﴾ [Yunus: 96], ﴿even if every sign should come to them until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 97]. The word "until" (*hatta*) indicates a limit. Allah, may He be exalted, thus limited their faith to the time of seeing the painful punishment, which is only the punishment of the Hereafter, for it is that which is described as painful. He, may He be exalted, negated their faith before that. Therefore their intentional faith before that is impossible by the text of this verse.

Once these two principles are established, let us return to what this scholar (*al-habr*) said about Pharaoh in *al-Futuhat al-Makkiyya* and in *al-Fusus*. What he mentioned in *al-Futuhat*, when he mentioned the levels of the people of the Fire within it, is that Pharaoh is among the people of the Fire, for he said in this discussion: "Like Pharaoh and his likes," and he assigned for him and them a specific level of the Fire in which they will be eternal. He indicated his disbelief in another place in it when he mentioned this hadith: "I seek refuge in You from You." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought refuge from the station of union (*ittihad*) in which Pharaoh was, which is his saying: ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24]. According to this indication and what preceded it, Pharaoh is a disbeliever in his view, as he is in the view of the common people. According to this, there is no difficulty and no discussion.

What remains is the question of Pharaoh's faith and salvation from the standpoint of the evidence. This is merely an examination with those who held definitively that he was a disbeliever, and they do not have this certainty, since the Qur'anic evidence indicates the opposite. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe..."﴾ [Yunus: 90], the verse. Here Pharaoh mentioned faith three times: twice concerning the Divine Presence, and the last one encompasses him, and faith in Musa when he said: ﴿And I am of the Muslims﴾ [Yunus: 90]. No one is a Muslim except one who combines faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Then our shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: In *al-Futuhat* and *al-Fusus* there is what amounts to this: that his faith was not at the time of despair, neither according to his school nor according to the school of those who agree with him, nor according to the school of others. As for the first, his faith was at the sight of worldly punishment, not at his death, and faith at the sight of worldly punishment is not considered despair according to him and according to a group. As for the second, Pharaoh's statement was not made at his despair from worldly life, for he knew that whoever believed in what the people of Musa believed in would share in the dry path that was for the believers, and he had shared with them in their faith. So the dominant assumption or certainty in his mind was the special treatment accorded to the believers, and the witnessing of it. He did not know Allah's sunnah in His creation, that worldly destruction is inevitable for one whose condition is like this, and worldly destruction does not indicate the absence of salvation in the Hereafter, which is evident. Accordingly, his faith was not at the time of despair according to both schools: the first with certainty, and the second according to what appears. It is not far-fetched that he was hoping for salvation with certainty, because of the general participation (in the dry path). This is so, and the school of this gnostic peculiar to him is to build on the breadth of Divine mercy and to take the apparent meanings of the verses. Nevertheless, when he discussed the question of Pharaoh's faith and salvation, alongside those who held the opposite of both, he said: Suspending judgment (*al-waqf*) on the question of Pharaoh's faith is safer, because of what has spread among people generally about his wretchedness. This is clear from him that he was examining his faith and salvation from the apparent wording of the Qur'anic text as an examination, not as one certain of them. End of the summary.

[p-3395] Then He, may He be exalted, informed of what He bestowed upon the Children of Israel following the blessing of their deliverance from their enemy and his destruction, and their failure to thank Him for it and to fulfill its rights, with His saying:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[93] ﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement, and provided them with good things. And they did not differ until knowledge had come to them. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾

﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾: the place is idafa-attributed to truthfulness (sidq), because it is the habit of the Arabs, when they praise something, to attribute it to truthfulness, saying: "a man of truth (rajul sidq)" and "a foot of truth (qadam sidq)." And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿an entrance of truth﴾ [al-Isra' 17:80] and ﴿an exit of truth﴾ [al-Isra' 17:80], when the qualifier is a suitable one for the intended purpose. It is as though they noticed that everything that is thought well of is truthful.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and provided them with good things﴾, these are the manna and the quail (al-manna wa'l-salwa) during the wandering (al-tih) and after it, from what overflowed upon them from the land which flows with milk and honey. ﴿And they did not differ until knowledge had come to them﴾, i.e., they did not split into various schools regarding the matter of their religion, except after knowledge had come to them, the decisive knowledge that removes every doubt, which is what was before them of the Revelation that they recite. That is: it was not their due to differ, since Allah had made clear to them and removed confusion from them. A parallel to this verse in censuring them for their differing is His saying: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah 98:4], and His saying, majestic is His remembrance: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rebellion among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:19]. In it is the greatest deterrent and the most mighty admonition against differing in religion and splitting within it.

﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾: i.e., He will distinguish the one in the right from the one in falsehood by salvation and destruction.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[94] ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. Certainly the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.﴾

﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ — that is, of the stories of Moses, Pharaoh and the Children of Israel. ﴿Then ask those who have been reading the Scripture﴾ — that is, the Torah — ﴿before you﴾, for it is with them in agreement with what was revealed to you. ﴿Certainly the truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ — that is, those who doubt that it has been sent down from Him.

Caution (tanbih):

It is not to be understood from this verse that doubt was established for him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, for the truth of a conditional statement (al-shartiyyah) does not require that its condition occur, as in your saying: "If the number five is even, it is divisible into two equal parts." The secret (al-sirr) in such statements is the multiplying of proofs and strengthening them, so that the strength of certainty increases, the heart is reassured, and the breast is calmed. For this reason, the Exalted has greatly multiplied in His Book the establishing of the proofs of Tawhid, prophethood and the Return. Or the secret is the reasoning toward confirming what was related and citing what is in the earlier Scripture, and that the Qur'an confirms what is in it. Or it is describing the rabbis as firmly rooted in knowledge, regarding the soundness of what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, as an allusion against the polytheists. Or it is stirring up the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and urging him so that his certainty increases, as the Friend (al-Khalil), may the blessings of Allah be upon him, said: ﴿But so that my heart may be at rest﴾ [al-Baqarah: 260]. It has also been narrated that "when this verse was revealed, he (ﷺ) said: 'I do not doubt, and I will not ask.'" It was recorded by ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir from Qatadah. Or the address is to him (ﷺ) while the intended meaning is others, in the manner of: "It is you I mean, but hear, O neighbour" (iyyaka aʿni wa-isma'i ya jarah). In this there is a power of impact on hearts beyond which there is nothing more, like a sultan addressing his governor in his town in the presence of its people with his awesome instructions and commands, which has a greater effect on souls. Or the address is to everyone who hears: that is, "If you, O listener, are in doubt about what We have sent down through the tongue of Our Prophet to you..." This is supported by His saying afterward: ﴿Say: O people, if you are in doubt about my religion﴾ [Yunus: 104], as if He indicated that those mentioned at the beginning of the verse symbolically are those mentioned explicitly afterward. And in the verse there is an admonition that whoever is struck by a doubt concerning the religion should hasten to resolve it by consulting the scholars who point to the truth.

And His, exalted is He, words:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[95] ﴿And do not be among those who deny the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers.﴾

﴿And do not be among those who deny the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers.﴾ This too is of the mode of stirring up, inflaming, and making firm. Some scholars have laid down a principle here, saying: a prohibition concerning anything, if it is addressed to one who is already engaged in it, its meaning is to abandon it; and if it is addressed to someone else, its meaning is to remain steadfast in its absence, and that it not proceed from him in the future, as is the case here. —End of quote— or the last two aspects mentioned before this may also come here.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[96] ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe.﴾ [97] ﴿Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 97]

﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ means: His noble word and His command concerning their punishment, as He said: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 13] ﴿will not believe﴾ ﴿Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 97], meaning: like the practice of the family of Pharaoh and their likes. That is: at the sight of the punishment the obligation is lifted, so their faith will not benefit them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[96] ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe.﴾ [97] ﴿Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 97]

﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ means: His noble word and His command concerning their punishment, as He said: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 13] ﴿will not believe﴾ ﴿Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 97], meaning: like the practice of the family of Pharaoh and their likes. That is: at the sight of the punishment the obligation is lifted, so their faith will not benefit them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 98:

(p-3398) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[98] ﴿Why was there not a town that believed and whose faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾

﴿Why was there not a town that believed﴾, meaning: Why was there not a town among the destroyed towns that believed before witnessing the punishment, and did not delay its faith until the moment of witnessing it, as Pharaoh did? In this specification there is a sense of reproach. ﴿And whose faith benefited it﴾, by God accepting it from them and removing the punishment from them because of it. ﴿Except the people of Yunus﴾, meaning: but his people ﴿when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time﴾, meaning: until their appointed terms.

Furthermore, it has been permitted that the sentence be understood in the sense of negation, since the particle of exhortation (hal/lawla) implies its meaning, so the exception is then connected (muttasil), because what is intended by "towns" is their inhabitants, as if He had said: No people of a town among the disobedient towns believed so that their faith benefited them, except the people of Yunus. And the reading in the nominative case as a substitute (badal) supports this.

It is narrated that Yunus, peace be upon him, was sent by God to Nineveh, in the land of Mosul. It was a great city, three days' journey in extent, and it was the capital of the lands of the Assyrians. Its builder was Ashur or Ninus son of Nimrod, and both were of the descendants of the children of Noah. It was among the oldest and most famous cities of the world. The pagan historians describe it as having walls one hundred feet high and a circumference of sixty miles, and it was fortified with fifteen hundred towers, each of which was two hundred feet long. It is said that its people numbered about six hundred thousand. The successors of Nimrod in this city worked to beautify it and expand its construction, and the power of the Assyrians grew in those days until most of the kingdoms of Asia submitted to them. Thus they became tyrannical and rebellious, and whenever they gained victory in their raids they would immerse themselves in plunder and injustice. So God sent to them Yunus, peace be upon him, whose name in Hebrew is (Yunan), to warn them that, because of their disbelief and their committing of destructive sins, punishment would befall them after forty days, and Nineveh would be overturned upon them. Then Yunus went out from among them and camped in the open country. When they lost him and the word of Yunus reached their ruler, (p-3399) they feared the descent of the punishment with which they had been warned. So God cast faith and repentance into the heart of their ruler, and he descended from his throne, cast off his robe, wrapped himself in sackcloth, sat on the dust, and believed in God, and all the people of Nineveh believed. He ordered that it be proclaimed in Nineveh that there should be a fast, so that no one should taste food or drink, that the animals should not graze nor be watered, and that the people should wear sackcloth, both young and old, and that they should gather in one open place, proclaiming the glorification of God, turning to Him, seeking His forgiveness, and repenting of the wrongdoing and sins they had committed previously, and that they should bring their children, their relatives and their livestock with them. They did so, humbled themselves before God, submitted to His majesty, and asked Him to lift from them the punishment with which their prophet had warned them. When He knew from them the sincerity of their hearts, and their repentance and remorse for what had passed of them, He removed the punishment from them and had mercy on them. The account of Yunus in (Surat al-Saffat) will come with more detail than what is here.

Notes:

The first: Some exegetes relate here that the punishment hung over them, enveloped them, began to circle above their heads, and the sky became covered with black cloud, and similar things. There is no clarification of this in the revelation, nor in the authentic Sunnah, and whoever claimed it seems to have understood it from the word (We removed/kashafna), which is not explicit in this.

Al-Qurtubi said: The meaning of ﴿We removed from them the punishment of disgrace﴾ is the punishment that Yunus had promised would descend upon them, not that they saw it at that time. So there is no particularity in it, as is narrated from Qatada, that this removal did not occur for any nation except the people of Yunus specifically, for the punishment did not befall them, but they saw its sign.

The second: The verse contains an indication that no town as a whole believed in its prophet sent to it, among all the other towns, following his mission and warning, except the people of Yunus; the rest were, all or most of them, accustomed to denial, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We did not send before you a warner into a town except that its affluent ones said: Indeed we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]

(p-3400) And in the authentic hadith: "The prophets were shown to me. A prophet would pass by with a great multitude of people, and a prophet with a man, and a prophet with two men, and a prophet with no one with him."

The third: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Caution does not avert destiny, but supplication averts destiny, and this is in the Book of God: ﴿except the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed﴾, the verse.

Abu al-Shaykh narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Supplication averts the decree, and it has descended from the sky. Recite if you wish: ﴿except the people of Yunus﴾, the verse.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Aisha, traced to the Prophet, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except the people of Yunus, when they believed﴾, that he, peace be upon him, said: "They supplicated" — thus in (al-Iklil).

And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the Lord's words:

[99] ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them, entirely. So would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾

﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them﴾ — meaning, to the extent that none of them would deviate from it. ﴿Entirely﴾ — meaning, united upon faith, not differing concerning it. That is: but He does not will it, because it contradicts the wisdom upon which the foundation of creation (takwin) and legislation (tashri') is built. ﴿So would you compel the people﴾ — meaning, to that which God has not willed from them. ﴿Until they become believers﴾ — meaning, this is not incumbent upon you, nor is it your responsibility, as in His words, exalted is He: (p-3401) ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 272]. In it is consolation for him ﷺ and relief for his heart from what he was eager for regarding their faith, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3]. ﴿For God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, so let not your soul expire in regret over them﴾ [Fatir: 8].

Therefore He, exalted is He, said:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[100] ﴿No soul could believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not reason.﴾

﴿No soul could believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ meaning, by His will and His enabling success (tawfiq). So do not exhaust yourself in seeking their guidance, for it rests with Allah. ﴿And He places defilement﴾ meaning, abandonment (khidhlan), ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾ meaning, His proofs and His evidences, because of the sealing (tab') upon their hearts.

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[101] ﴿Say: "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe."﴾

﴿Say: "Look"﴾ i.e., reflect. ﴿at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ i.e., of the signs that point to His Oneness and the perfection of His power. Al-Suyuti said: The verse is evidence for the obligation of reflective inquiry (nazar) and personal striving (ijtihad), and for abandoning blind imitation (taqlid) in matters of belief. ﴿But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ i.e., neither the signs nor the warning messengers benefit those who do not believe, or "warnings" means the admonitions. The "ma" here is either interrogative or negative.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 102:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[102] ﴿Are they waiting for anything but like the days of those who passed away before them? Say, "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among the waiting."﴾

﴿Are they waiting for anything but like the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ That is, like His days (ayyam, i.e. events, or "days" in the sense of the occurrences of the Almighty's dealings) with them, just as it is said "the days of the Arabs" (ayyam al-Arab) for their battles, using a term of time to refer to what happened in it, as "al-maghrib" is used for the prayer that occurs at it. ﴿Say﴾, that is, as a threat to them, ﴿Then wait﴾, that is, see what your outcome will be, ﴿indeed, I am with you among the waiting.﴾ And His saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[103] ﴿Then We shall deliver Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus it is an obligation upon Us that We deliver the believers.﴾

﴿Then We shall deliver Our messengers﴾ is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon an omitted element known from the context, as if it were said: We destroy the nations, then We deliver Our messengers who were sent to them. ﴿And those who have believed. Thus it is an obligation upon Us that We deliver the believers﴾, i.e., from every hardship and punishment. And His words, Exalted is He:

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[104] ﴿Say: "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die. And I have been commanded to be among the believers."﴾

﴿Say: "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion, then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die."﴾ The address was given with the generic noun (ism al-jins), namely "mankind," and introduced with the vocative particle (harf al-tanbih), in order to generalize the delivery of the message and to show the complete care given to the matter that was conveyed to them. He expressed their state as "doubt" rather than "certainty" to indicate that this is the furthest that doubt could possibly reach, since the clarity of its soundness and the proof of its truth are more evident than the sun at the brightness of midday. He placed the abandonment of worshipping others before the worship of Him, exalted is He, to indicate that they opposed him from the very beginning. And in singling out "causing to die" (al-tawaffi) for mention in connection with them, there is a threat that is not hidden, for nothing is more severe for them than death. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the believers﴾, meaning: with the highest degree of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness).

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[105] ﴿And that I should set my face toward the religion, upright, and never be of those who associate others with God.﴾

﴿And that I should set my face toward the religion, upright﴾ — i.e., inclining away from the false religions.

Two subtle points:

The first: "setting the face toward the religion" is a metaphor (kinaya) for directing the self entirely toward the worship of God, exalted is He, and turning away from all else. For when one wishes to look closely at something, he sets his face opposite it, such that he does not turn right or left; for if he turned, the facing would be broken. Therefore the face is used as a metaphor for devoting one's action wholly to the religion. So "the face" here means the essence: that is, direct your essence and your entire self to the religion. The lam is then connected to the verb (ṣila).

The second: the clause "and that I should set" (wa-an aqim) is coordinated (ʿatf) upon "that I should be" (an akūna). It was permissible to report the complement of "an" (that) in the imperative form, because there is no difference in the complement of a harfi relative pronoun between a request (ṭalab) and a statement (khabar), since the purpose is to connect it with something that carries the meaning of the verbal noun (maṣdar), and this is achieved by any verb. Some have said: here there is an implied verb, i.e., "and it was revealed to me that I should set," and that "an" may be a verbal particle (maṣdariyya) and explanatory (mufassira), because the implied verb carries the meaning of saying without its letter; then he preferred this view on the ground that the unease of the coordination disappears in it, and the address in "your face" falls in its proper place. It was refuted: an explanatory clause may not be omitted, and there is no unease in this coordination, and the matter of the address is easy, since it is for the sake of considering the reported speech and the matter mentioned with it. Thus in (al-ʿInaya).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And never be of those who associate others with God﴾ is an incitement and urging to him to worship God, exalted is He, and a prohibition to others, as has preceded.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 106:

(p-3404) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[106] ﴿And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you nor harm you. For if you should do so, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And do not invoke﴾ i.e., do not worship ﴿besides Allah that which can neither benefit you﴾, i.e., neither in this world nor in the Hereafter if you worship it, ﴿nor harm you﴾ if you do not worship it. ﴿For if you should do so﴾, i.e., worship it, ﴿then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who harm themselves, or who place a matter in other than its proper place. ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13].

The discussion of the words of His Exalted Saying:

[107] ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him. And if He intends for you good, there is none to repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whomever He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him. And if He intends for you good, there is none to repel His bounty. He causes it to reach whomever He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ When Exalted Allah forbade the worship of idols and described them as being unable to benefit or harm, He made clear that He, glory be to Him, is the One who harms and benefits. If He touches someone with harm, none can remove it except Him alone, not any other being. How then [could it be] with inanimate matter that has no awareness? Likewise, if He intends good, no one can repel what He wills of His bounty and kindness. How then [could it be] with idols? So He alone is the Real, and thus worship should be directed to Him instead of them.

Subtleties (lata'if):

It has been said: He mentioned "touching" (mass) in the first and "intending" (irada) in the second, to indicate that the two are interrelated: whatever He intends, He causes to reach, and whatever He causes to reach happens only by His will. However, He stated explicitly in each of them one of the two matters, as an indication that good is intended for its own sake by Him, Exalted, whereas harm only came as a recompense for their deeds and is not intended for its own sake; therefore, the word "intention" was not used with regard to it.

It has also been said: He aimed at brevity, so in each of the two contrasting clauses He mentioned what indicates the intention of the like of it in the other, since the context requires emphasizing both encouragement and warning. This is a type of rhetorical device called ihtibak (interlocking).

Abu al-Su'ud said: Moreover, He has explicitly stated "reaching" (isabah) where He said "He causes it to reach" (yusibu bihi), to show the complete care regarding the aspect of good, as is indicated by the omission of the exception in it. That is: He causes to reach, by His vast bounty that encompasses whatever He intends for you of good.

Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek good all your life, and expose yourselves to the breezes (nafahat) of your Lord, for Allah has breezes of His mercy, by which He causes whomever He wills of His servants to be reached. And ask Him to cover your faults and to secure your frightened moments." He narrated the like of it from Abu Hurayrah.

And the saying of His Exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 10, verse 108:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[108] ﴿Say: "O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided, it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is guided; and whoever goes astray, it is only against it that he goes astray. And I am not over you a guardian."﴾

﴿Say﴾, i.e., to those disbelievers and sinners, after the proofs of tawhid (Divine Oneness), prophethood and the Resurrection had reached them and you had warned them. ﴿O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿So whoever is guided﴾, i.e., by believing in it, ﴿it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is guided﴾, i.e., the benefit of his being guided belongs to him alone. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾, i.e., by disbelieving in it, ﴿it is only against it that he goes astray﴾, i.e., the burden of straying falls upon it. The meaning is: there remains for you, with the coming of the truth, no excuse, and no proof against Allah; so whoever chooses guidance and following the truth has benefited only himself, and whoever prefers straying has harmed only himself. In this is the clearing of the station of the Message from any taint of a purpose returning to him, peace be upon him, of bringing benefit or harm, as is suggested by the attribution of the coming to the truth, without any indication that this occurs through him. (Related by Abu al-Su'ud.)

﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾, i.e., a keeper to whom your affairs have been entrusted; I am only a bringer of good tidings and a warner.

(p-3406) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[109] ﴿And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges; and He is the best of judges.﴾

﴿And follow what is revealed to you﴾, i.e., in conveying it, even if they do not accept guidance from it. ﴿And be patient﴾, i.e., over their harm in calling to the faith. ﴿Until Allah judges﴾, i.e., judges in your favor against them with victory and dominance. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾. And He has indeed judged, and He willed their killing and capture on the Day of Badr, and to Him belongs the command, before and after.
